characters.name: Finn the Human
characters.description: The intrepid human boy and one of the two lead characters of the series. Hyperactive with a love of adventure and good deeds. That thing on his head is actually a hat. Originally 12 years old, he gets older as the series progresses. 10-Minute Retirement: In "Freak City", Finn goes through one of these after getting turned into a foot, during which he memorably goes intoAuto-Tunedsong. Though it's more than thirty seconds than ten minutes. The later episode "Davey" is built around this also, with him developing a split personality. Adoption Angst: Finn was raised by a family of talking dogs after the parents found him as a baby. Though he loves his adoptive parents, Margaret and Joshua, he also angsts over not knowing where he came from or who his birth parents are, all the more punctuated by the fact that he's never met another human being. When he does eventually meet his biological father, he is disappointed to find that Martin does not actually care about him. Thankfully, meeting his biological mother goes over much better. Aesop Amnesia:Fionna and Cakeshows Finncontinuing his previous habits of relying on adventuring to address emotional trauma instead of actually dealing with it. When he sees Simon in a depressed existential crisis over losing Betty and being stuck in a world he doesn't belong in, he decides to take Simon on an adventure. During the adventure, Simon brings back some past memories with Betty, though Finn tells Simon not to talk about sad stuff, believing it is better to forget about it. It's clear that Jake's death has caused him to regress to his previous mentality of repressing emotional trauma, given how Finn outright admits to Jake in the afterlife that a part of him was always waiting to die to reunite with Jake again. Alternate Self: Unusually for any series, the Finn we meet at the beginning of the series becomes Farmworld Finn after Prismo grants his wish in "Finn the Human". characters.name: Jake the Dog
characters.description: Finn's chummy, shape-shifting bulldog friend (not pet) and foster-brother. He is more laid back than Finn, but also enjoys adventure. He sometimes gives Finn brotherly advice, but it is not often helpful. Action Dad: He sires five pups with Lady Rainicorn in "Jake the Dad". Actor Allusion: His voice actor was another magical talking dog. Animalistic Abomination: While he's introduced as a dog with stretching and shapeshifting powers, his parents were ordinary dogs. It turns out he was spawned from a bump that appeared on his father Joshua's head after he was bitten by a shapeshifting monster. Ambiguously Bi: While Jake is unambiguously attracted to Lady Rainicorn, more than a few of his comments to guys have hinted at attraction that is more than just platonic, outright declaring love a couple of times such as when he blatantly admits to having a secret crush on Billy and the fact that he occasionally dates Cinnamon Bun while shapeshifting and putting on a bow to be his "girlfriend". There's also his very strong attachment to Prismo, and more than a few comments shared between the two can be seen as romantic crushes or platonic confessions.

characters.name: Princess Bubblegum
characters.description: The young-looking princess and current ruler of the Candy Kingdom. She cares deeply about her citizens. She's also a giant nerd, said to engage in "every branch of geekdom", but not (as far as we can tell) in theCosplay Otaku Girlway— she's more of a math and science whiz. She's also a hybrid of human DNA and bubblegum DNA (which Finnfinds a-TRACTT-ive~!),despite bubblegum not having DNA, hence her name. She's close friends with Finn, who seems to have a crush on her (however much hetries to deny it), but she brusquelyrefuses any romantic advances. She finds Jake funny and charming, and has a complicated relationship with Marceline. Although she lookssweet, and is, in general, rather nice, she is actually quite quick to anger, and her wrath isbest avoided. She also speaks German, apparently. The second season reveals her first name is Bonnibel, and her true age has also been revealed:827. Abdicate the Throne:After the King of Ooo convinces the rest of the Candy Kingdom to vote him as Princess, PB storms off in frustration with a "If he wants it, he can have it" attitude. She spends the next little while effectively treating it as vacation knowingKoOwillbe such a miserable rulerthey'll eventually get sick of him and take her back. As she points out when she has to boss some Banana Guards around in an emergency, the Candy Kingdom is a monarchy, so a democratic vote means squat in the first place.At the end of Season 2 ofFionna and CakeBubblegum has afull on sobbing breakdownover nearly killing Finn, with Marceline suggesting Bubblegum needed to take a break. She flings her tiara onto Pepper Mint's head and he's later seen in Huntress Wizard's magic class saying he needs to learn about agriculture for "his" people, implying she had given him the title. Given that he's still wearing the tiara in "Together Again" decades later, it seems Bubblegum's break was either still ongoing, made permanent, or she had taken another break to mourn Finn. characters.name: BMO
characters.description: BMO, pronouncedBeemo, is Finn and Jake'scuteAnimate InanimateVideo Gamesystem. A bit of a rebel and with a tendency to get lost in his imagination, Beemo sometimes enjoys turning up his volume too loud and running out of batteries during a game. Speaks with a Korean accent, and looks like cross between aGame Boy,Macintoshand aVectrex.Was built by pre-Mushroom War robotics engineer Moseph Maestro Giovanni to be a companion and best friend to the son he never had and eventually sent into the world by said inventor to "Be More" and find a family. Adaptational Badass: Downplayed in thePirates of the Enchiridionvideo game, while BMO's arsenal in that game is best suited for being aSupport Party Member, she's still tough enough to keep up with Finn, Jake, and Marceline in fighting alongside them, something that would be difficult for them to pull off in the show. Ambiguous Gender: Typically referred to as a "he", but was referred to as "M'lady" by Finn in the season 3 premiere. However, he called himself a boy in "Five Short Graybles". And in "Five More Short Graybles" her alter ego claimed to be a "real baby girl". The version of him seen in the Fionna and Cake stories looksexactly the same, so that's no help either.In thePixel Princessescomic BMO wishes to become a princess and is eventually made an honorary one — and theGrand Finalereveals that in the far futurethey have become the legendary King of Ooo.TheWonderConQ&A panel confirmed that BMO is genderfluid, and both male and female pronouns apply.In theMunchkin Adventure Timecard game, every character has a card with two sides, depicting the normal character and gender-bent Fionna and Cake counterpart (as inMunchkin, your character's STARTING gender is the same as your own). While BMO's card has two sides and two different pictures, no gender can be derived from them, and the card outright states that BMO ignores any gender-related stuff in the game. characters.name: Marceline the Vampire Queen
characters.description: The queen of the vampires(by default as she killed all the other vampires, including the king). Known to be extremely unempathetic but never cruel, simply doing whatever she pleases even at the expense of others. Was alive at the time of the apocalyptic 'mushroom war'. Usually decked out in punk-rock apparel. She generally tries to be cool and rather unfeeling, she harbors a very broken spirit due to loneliness in living forever, among other things. Whenever her more sensitive or emotional side is shown, she gets angry. She and fellow immortal Ice King also share a long and painful history together, and she spends much of her time finding and moving into new houses to avoid him, until the events of "I Remember You". Absent Animal Companion: Marceline has a pet poodle named Shwabl, who's been her companion since before she was turned into a vampire. The book "The Enchiridion & Marcy's Super Secret Scrapbook" reveals that when she turned, she accidentally sucked the pink out of Shwabl's fur and nearly killed him, but was able to bring him back as a half-ghost thanks to a spell from the Enchiridion. In the show however, Schwabl only appears in the background at her house in a handful of episodes. Action Girl: She can definitely handle herself in wild situations. Although her lazy side makes it so she doesn't get to show it off much. Affably Evil: When she was an antagonist (which lasted for about one episode, not counting her trickery in "Henchman"); since then she's settled into a more neutral type of personality with a generalLack of Empathy, being more Affably Amoral than anything.

characters.name: Lady Rainicorn
characters.description: An odd-looking but beautiful, flying half-rainbow-half-unicorn creature. Also Jake's girlfriend and as of season 5, the mother of their children. She only speaks Korean, which Jake and Princess Bubblegum, but not Finn, understands. Action Girl: She's a "rowdy queen" who's not afraid to go into combat. Badass Adorable: She's able to keep up with Finn and Jake in "My Two Favorite People", and she even has to save Finn from the army of lake monsters. Surprising, considering she looks like a little girl's toy. Beta Couple: Jake has a fairly stable long-term relationship with Lady Rainicorn, contrasting Finn dealing with unrequited crushes. Bilingual Bonus: Given that she only speaks Korean, this is inevitable.

characters.name: Lumpy Space Princess
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: To Finn, who would be put off by her advances. Attention Whore: She crashes Tree Trunk's wedding dressed in a wedding gown of her own, saying that everyone is ready to pay attention toher. Big Eater: Has been this on multiple occasions, constantly shown eating large portions of food, even rivaling Jake in this department. Big "NO!":Played for Laughswhen Finn and Jake spill her beans in "Heat Signature". Bratty Teenage Daughter: She tells Finn that she "lumping hate[s]" her parents, and that her "parents are horrible idiots."

characters.name: Tree Trunks
characters.description: A cute little elephant with the personality of a senile old woman. She loves apples and baking apple pie. Animals Not to Scale: She's a lot smaller than an elephant should be. "Ring of Fire" reveals that this is because she's from Tiny Mammal Kingdom, whereallanimals are the same size. Babies Make Everything Better: She seemingly changes her mind about asking Mr. Pig for a divorce when Finn leaves the baby-fied Lich as aDoorstop Babyfor them to adopt. Cloudcuckoolander: More due to senility. She occasionally gets names confused, such as Ice King being "Ice Cream" or Earl of Lemongrab as "Lemoncarb". Cool Old Lady: She may be old and slightly senile, but she's still a great friend to Finn and Jake and can still adventure with them at times.

characters.name: Flame Princess
characters.description: The princess of the Fire Kingdom; who is made out of fire. Beneath her innocent exterior is a deeply destructive and unpredictable personality, with a terrible temper. She has no perspective on the norms of the world and doesn't seem to understand what is right or wrong, likely due to being sheltered by her father. At the end of the third season, she inadvertentlybecomes Finn's new love interest. By the fifth season, it's clear that she's growing into a more settled personality, having spent time interacting with the world. She eventually usurps the position of ruler of the Flame Kingdom from her father. Action Girl: She'sincrediblypowerful and destructive. Always Chaotic Evil:Subverted. She thinks destroying things is fun — but only evil things, as mentioned at the end of "Vault of Bones". While the rest of her races are played straight, she tends to handle situations like a'90s Anti-Hero. However, she will not, under any circumstances, willingly hurther boyfriend. Ambiguously Evil: Was this for a good while until the truth came out: she is not truly evil after all, just emotionally disturbed due to being locked in a lamp most of her life because of her having world-destroying powers. However, her father, The Flame King, does state that she and everyone else in the Flame Kingdomareevil, but spending enough time with a good person can potentiallychange her over to the side of good(although she'd sufferpenalties to her experience for doing so). Then again, her father doeslove being evil, and after he was overthrown the Flame Kingdom is a lot better. Amicable Exes:She and Finn break up in season 5 after Finn manipulated her into fighting with the Ice King and accidentally destroys the Ice Kingdom in the process, and are on pretty bad terms after that. In "Earth and Water" they finally make some sort of amends and agree to stay friends, but even then is still incredibly awkward, due to, in no small part, Finn still having feelings for her. This trope is finally played

characters.name: Peppermint Butler
characters.description: Princess Bubblegum's loyal servant. Best friends with Death. Will probably eat your flesh while you are sleeping. Affably Evil: Despite being confirmed to be evil, he does still stay by Princess Bubblegum's side and is on mutually good terms with Finn and Jake. Almighty Janitor: A simple butler, yet dropping his name will get you an immediate favor from Death itself. Ambiguously Evil: In addition to his association with Death, aFreeze-Frame Bonusin "Return to the Nightosphere" shows a picture of him playing golf with Marceline's Dad.In "You Made Me" Peppermint Butler suddenly becomes very nervous when Finn suggests using PB's Aura Visualizer to view his aura.Finn: I want to see Peppermint Butler's aura!Peppermint Butler: *laughs nervously* Youdon'twant to see that.InThe Suitorhe technically drops the Ambiguousness by blatantly summoning a demon to gain power and is referred to as Dark One by a Gumball Guardian. However, the Gumball Guardians don't react to that (instead one of them simply interupts him due to PB being in the lab for weeks) and he is not seen doing anything particularly evil with that power, so it might be"in name only".As of "Nemesis", it's no longer ambiguous. He IS evil, it's just that his interests and schemes never go against the Candy Kingdom or anyone else on the heroes' side so he never comes into conflict with them. In "You Made Me" Peppermint Butler suddenly becomes very nervous when Finn suggests using PB's Aura Visualizer to view his aura.Finn: I want to see Peppermint Butler's aura!Peppermint Butler: *laughs nervously* Youdon'twant to see that.

characters.name: Betty Grof
characters.description: The fiancée of Simon Petrikov, aka the Ice King. She lived on Earth before the apocalypse untilTime Travelbrought her to the present-day Land of Ooo. Accidental Hero:Her high-risk plan to return Simon to normal also resulted in Ice Queen/Simone being cured of the Ice Crown curse.In her debut episode, she restores the crown's magic to prevent Simon from dying ofRapid Aging. This, in turn, indirectly saves the world of Fionna stored in his mind.Her permafusion withGOLBallows her to canonize the world of Fionna. Her high-risk plan to return Simon to normal also resulted in Ice Queen/Simone being cured of the Ice Crown curse. In her debut episode, she restores the crown's magic to prevent Simon from dying ofRapid Aging. This, in turn, indirectly saves the world of Fionna stored in his mind. Her permafusion withGOLBallows her to canonize the world of Fionna.

characters.name: Huntress Wizard
characters.description: A female warrior wizard who starts out living in Wizard City, but abandons it for a secluded life in nature. Action Girl: Of course. Why else would she have such a name? In her first appearance, she's facing off against other wizards in combat, and her first appearance as a real cast member has her helping Finn subdue a rampaging boar. HerImprobable Aiming Skillswith energy arrows prove she's spent a lot of time practicing. The Ageless: In Season 2 ofFionna and Cake, Huntress Wizard hasn't visibly aged since the events of the main series. Her childhood flashback, told in the framing of an old fairy tale, implies she'sveryold indeed. Aloof Archer: Her signature weapon is a bow and arrow; she has a stoic, serious personality and is very independent. Always Save The Guy: Huntress Wizard goes to great lengths to save Finn’s life without considering the consequences. The first time she does this is when she accidentally injures The Heart of the Forest, and the second time is when she intentionally killsThe Cosmic Owl.

characters.name: Hunson Abadeer
characters.description: Abusive Parents:Played With. Hunson does care for Marceline, but at the same time, he's very selfish and impulsive, doing what he wants no matter how it might affect his daughter personally (such as eating fries that he knew had significance to her, or forcing her into a position she does not want), and constantly ignores her own input whenever they do talk and often doesn't apologize for any of his actions towards her. Overall, his abuse comes from ignorance/alien morality than anything malicious. Affably Evil: To Finn and Jake in his second appearance, but arguably and surprisinglynotMarceline, who he blatantly lies to and manipulates even under the guise of an eccentric but caring father. Granted, he does love and care about her, but is pretty lousy at explaining it. This is played more straight in "Marcy & Hunson"."I'm bad, but I'm notsobad, right?" Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: While he tries to be supportive in "Marcy & Hunson" by attending Marceline's concert, he only ends up making a scene and embarrassing her. Artifact of Doom: He owns an amulet made of concentrated evil, whichgives the wearer a nice suitand transforms him or her into a ruthlessEldritch Abomination. Badass in a Nice Suit: Pilfers souls, rules the Ooo equivalent of the underworld and may rival the Lich himself, all while dressed in a snappy suit and tie. It's also invoked, since anyone who wears the amulet gains the suit and tie along with the pure evil.

characters.name: Earl of Lemongrab
characters.description: A very loud and extremely uptight lemon drop man created in a lab by Princess Bubblegum in case she was ever unable to rule the kingdom. The first one of the princess's experiments gone wrong, he has a... "special" way of thinking and looking at the world. He lives with a clone of himself (so aptly named Lemongrab 2) and their Lemon Children/Subjects in Castle Lemongrab. He eventually became a power-hungry tyrant who ate his brother, but thanks to Lemonhope, he was defeated and PB combined the two Lemongrabs into Lemongrab 3, who has mellowed out. As Lemongrab 3, he becomes much more empathetic and retains at least some of his earlier incarnations' memories, if not all of them. 0% Approval Rating: As established in "You Made Me!", just abouteveryonein the Candy Kingdom completely despises him and vehemently protest against Princess Bubblegum's request that some of them go to Castle Lemongrab to keep him company. One Candy Person, Mr. Cupcake, actually goes so far as tobreak his own armjust to have an excuse not to hang out with Lemongrab. Averted asLemongrab 3, at least in his kingdom. Adipose Rex: "Too Old" and "Lemonhope" depicts him as being morbidly obese, possibly as a result of eating much of his brother. Abusive Dad: In "Too Old", Lemongrab becomes this when hegoes over completely to the dark side, especially toward Lemonhope. As Lemongrab 3, however, he becomes a verygood parent. All Crimes Are Equal: He treats extremely small offenses as if they were serious, terrible crimes.

characters.name: King of Ooo
characters.description: The king of the Land of Ooo... except not really. In reality, he's aCon Manwho claims to be the king of Ooo, and everybody believes him. He's legally able to perform marriages. He takes over as princess of the Candy Kingdom in the Season 6 finale, before being deposed at the end of "The Dark Cloud". 0% Approval Rating: The King of Ooo'sCaligulaattitude since he took over the Candy Kingdom finallybites him on the assin this episode when the Candy Peopleget fed up with his bullshitand revolt. Bonus Points for Crunchie knocking his assinto an open fire, causing him to melt into a puddle, and crawl away. Authority in Name Only: He doesn't seem to wield any real power at all. At least until he manages to usurp Princess Bubblegum's place in "Hot Diggity Doom". Bait-and-Switch: In his debut episode, he comes across as a pretty friendly, likeable guy when officiating Tree Trunks's wedding, with his worst flaw being that he broke out of jail out of the belief that Bubblegum would want his head on a platter (that and the vows stated both bride and groom would be his servants for five years, but it's rather easy to miss as the show doesn't bring attention to it). Subsequent appearances make it clear that King of Ooo is a greedy, selfish, and hedonistic man who is willing to lie, cheat, steal, and manipulate to get his way, and doesn't care who gets hurt as long as he benefits. Bavarian Fire Drill: It's implied that the only reason people even believed he was a king is simply that he acted like one.

characters.name: Martin Mertens
characters.description: Finn's father, trapped on the Citadel for unexplained reasons. He's freed during "Escape from the Citadel". Abusive Dad: In addition to his complete apathy towards Finn's existence within minutes of meeting him, he manipulates his son into healing him, immediately ditches him, and constantly attempts to use him to further his own goals. There are a few hints that he cares for Finn, but they are buried behind Martin's selfishness.Ironically, it was shown in the past that Martin was a very protective dad. Acrofatic: Martin's quite rotund but is very agile. Alliterative Name:MartinMertens. Ambiguous Situation:Whether Martin'sJerkassbehavior in the present is a result of his head injury and memory issues or him simply choosing to burn bridges after he believed his son died and returning to old behavior is ultimately up to the viewer to decide.

characters.name: GOLB
characters.description: A malevolent being who is the embodiment of chaos and all that is evil. Turns out he has had followers or such as some point... most notably the Lich. Abstract Eater: His equivalent to the digestive process breaks down things conceptually, reverting them to earlier states. This reverts Ice King back into Simon and the magic crown back into its original state of granting wishes. Almighty Idiot: Ambiguous, but he doesn't move with any sense of purpose untilBetty takes over his body, implying he has no mind of his own. Ambiguous Situation:It's not clear if he used to desire the death of all living things andBetty's dominance of their fusion changed thator if he never wanted it and the Lich was simply mistaken. Anthropomorphic Personification: Embodies discord and chaosolder than the universe.

characters.name: Hugo
characters.description: The Drift's lead scientist, a space elf trying to keep The Drift from falling apart. Big Bad: Of "BMO", being the one responsible for the Drift falling apart. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: While he plays the part of a benevolent scientist, he's actually nothing more than a corrupt executive that aims to steal The Drift's resources for himself and a select number of wealthy supporters. Broken Pedestal: Needless to say, Y5 loses all respect for Hugo after she uncovers hisEvil Plan. The Elites Jump Ship: His plan several times over has been to evacuate himself and his closest associates, plunder the place for whatever is useful to him, and repeat.

characters.name: Molto Larvo
characters.description: A fiery dragon who has terrified the glass kingdom for centuries. Big Bad: He's the main antagonist of "Obsidian". Evil Is Burning Hot: True to his name he's a molten mass of glass. When he slams a glass person with an arm, instead of shattering or crushing them the heat immediately flattens them into a puddle. Heel–Face Turn:Hearing Marceline's new song,Monster, allowed him to let go of the rage he was hanging onto and come to terms with his trauma; transforming him into a peaceful butterfly-like creature. Leaking Can of Evil: He was sealed away in a cavern near the glass kingdom, but the citizens occasionally entered to use his heat to heal their cracks. Once the seal begins weakening it sends out minions to try and take out Marceline before she can help seal it back up.

characters.name: New Death
characters.description: The son of Life and Death who has taken over as ruler of the Dead Worlds and the new Death himself. Alas, Poor Villain: Surprisingly, considering what an obnoxious jerk he is.In the final moments before his death, he realizes that the weapon used to kill him was given to them by his own mother, he lets out a confused and quiet "Mom?" as he covers his face, making him pitiable right before his end. All Deaths Final: He tries to end the cycle of reincarnation, which would result in this.This ultimately costs him his life, as it turned his mother Life against him and made her create a weapon toKill and Replacehim. Ambiguously Gay: Despite his claim that they are friends, his manner of speaking suggests something else, like in the scene where he whispers and kisses his hand, later revealed to be The Lich. He also has a pinup in his room of the Vampire King wearing only a towel. Bad Boss: He treats his minions like dirt; regularly insulting them and even killing one on a whim.

characters.name: Hana Abadeer
characters.description: A humanDistaff Counterpartof Hunson Abadeer, and Marshall's estranged mother. Abusive Parents: She passively-aggressively insults Marshall to his face multiple times, in the middle of a social gathering of the city's biggest names. Gary has none of it and outright calls her a bad mother for it.This is explored further in "The Butterfly and the River", where it's shown that she attempted to stifle his creative outbursts by ripping up his drawings. She grew impatient with him rocking his chair noisily to the point that she shoved a few dollars at him before kicking him out of her room. This has resulted in Marshall developing rejection anxiety and an unwillingness to open up his feelings in the present. She is also tracking Marshall by hiring a tracker to follow his every move. She does want the best for Marshall, but it's according toherbeliefs and most notably, without Marshall's input. She grew impatient with him rocking his chair noisily to the point that she shoved a few dollars at him before kicking him out of her room. This has resulted in Marshall developing rejection anxiety and an unwillingness to open up his feelings in the present. She is also tracking Marshall by hiring a tracker to follow his every move. She does want the best for Marshall, but it's according toherbeliefs and most notably, without Marshall's input. Accidental Misnaming: When being introduced to Gary by her son, Hana calls him "Gravy". Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: In her second encounter with Gary, she shows off the custom marble coffin she had made for Marshall in the family's mausoleum, which she had carved in Marshall's likeness. Marshall is understandably mortified, and even more so when Hana shows the coffin she has prepared for Gary (or whomever Marshall last ends up with before he dies).

characters.name: Witch Wizard
characters.description: A green wizard and the protector of the Heart of the Forest, who often takes the form of a giant green bear. Anti-Villain: She's a power hungry Wizard who has no issue killing trespassers or abusing Green Magic for herself, but she's more intent on giving herself power rather than being a malicious entity.When Huntress pleads to her to help her return to Ooo, she ultimately gives in, helping save Finn's life in the process. Ascended Extra: She goes from a random monster encountered by Finn and Simon in the first season to an actual character in the second. Big Bad Ensemble: She shares the role of Season 2's main villain with Queenie and Hana Abadeer, indirectly being the cause of Finn being fatally poisoned by the Heart of the Forest and also standing in the way of Huntress Wizard's attempts to procure a cure from it. She was immediately neutralized after the Heart of the Forest was crippled but she came back once more in the Undergrowth to stop Huntress Wizard from going back to Ooo. Big Bad Wannabe: At the same time, she's easily outmatched by both Finn and Huntress in a straight fight; Finn only got poisoned effectivelyby accidentdue to her throwing him into the Heart of the Forest and he was still able to choke her out afterwards.When she returns in the Undergrowth, she's gotten a power-up, but it's also aDeadly Upgradethat quickly burns through her to the point Huntress is able to defeat her just by realizing she isn't worth fighting and waiting for her to burn out enough to be restrained.This is justified, as she's not exactly a villain or craving the harm of other people, just someone who craves power.

characters.name: Ricardio
characters.description: And Now You Must Marry Me: In "Lady & Peebles", he tells Princess Bubblegum that he wants to be "united as man and wife" with her. Art Evolution: Compared to hisappearance◊in Season 1's "Ricardio the Heart Guy", his face looksmore detailed◊in Season 4's "Lady & Peebles", with visible irises, more realistic cheekbones than the bulging cheeks he had previously, and a more pronounced upper lip. Asshole Victim: Considering he stalked her and tried to cut out her heart, it's hard to feel bad when both Finn and Princess Bubblegum kick his butt and damn near kill him in the process. Ax-Crazy: He tries to cut out Princess Bubblegum's heart with broken bottles. Beat Still, My Heart: He's a guy who happens to be a living heart. It turns out that he used to be the heart of the Ice King, brought to life by a spell gone awry. He makes a second appearance much later on, setting up aWomb Level-like lair and replacing his limbs with muscular arms and legs...but still leaving his body exposed.

characters.name: Me-Mow
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: A sadistic assassin who gleefully loves her job — which involves killing people. Badass Adorable: Don't let her size fool you; she's quite deadly. Bounty Hunter: Resorts to hunting bounties after getting kicked out of the assassin guild. The Bus Came Back: Returns four seasons later after her initial appearance in "Angel Face" and one season later in "Elements".She also returns as part of Gumbald's army in the final season. Bus Crash:Her skull can be seen in the bird nest in "Together Again", confirming that she died before Finn did.

characters.name: Kee-Oth
characters.description: A demon who created the Demon Sword with his own blood, which was taken by Jake's father, Joshua. He really,reallywants his blood back. Big Red Devil: He looks like the stereotypical demon with a forked tongue, red skin, horns, pointy ears, bat-like wings, and pointy-tipped tail. Blood Magic: His power comes from his blood and the blood he drains from others. Finn uses this to trick him into killing himself. Didn't See That Coming: How he lost his demon blood in the first place was by using it to create the Demon Sword to cut the chain restraining him when Joshua left for the bathroom after drinking so much holy water. Upon gloating on his escape, Joshua swoops back in and splashes the holy water in his face, thus causing Kee-Oth to lose his demon blood. Dumb Muscle: He's decently powerful, but not very smart. Joshua, and later Finn, are able to outsmart him pretty easily.

characters.name: Oozers
characters.description: Humanoid creatures created in the aftermath of the Mushroom War, oozing green slime from all their orifices. They plagued Simon and young Marceline in their travels, and they're still around, awoken by PB, Finn, Jake and James. Always Chaotic Evil: Their presence is evil enough to cause the Gumball Guardians to awaken. Body Horror: They are all bloated and deformed, but some are worse than others, such as some with holes in their chests or limbs growing out of their mouths. Not Using the "Z" Word: They are never once referred to as zombies.Understandable,since the show has already introduced a totally different kind of zombieinSlumber Party Panic. Nuclear Mutant: A nasty result of the Mushroom War.

characters.name: Big Destiny
characters.description: The off-kilter leader of the Destiny Gang, a group of criminals in the Farmworld universe. Abusive Parents:Not only does Big Destiny "reward" his son Peanut by pushing him into a large crater, with the implications that the fall almost killed him, but he attempts to have Little Destiny burned alive when he learns that she's dating Finn's son Jay. The former act comes back to bite him in Fionna and Cake Season 2 as Peanut comes back to kill him. Asshole Victim:With how much of a bully and abusive jerk he is, it's hard to say that he didn't have his death at Peanut's hands coming. Back for the Dead:His return in Season 2 ofFionna and Cakeis in a Cosmic Owl croak dream. The moment he wakes up, his face is shredded by Peanut's wolf. Bald of Evil: He's shown to have a receding hairline by the time ofFionna and Cake, and is still no less of an evil jerk.

characters.name: Maja
characters.description: A.K.A The Sky Witch. She's the person Ash sold Hambo to in order to learn some useless spells. Marcie's since been trying to track her down to retrieve her doll. Aborted Arc: Her introduction was supposed to lead into the plot of an Adventure Time movie where she was meant to have a bigger role. But that ended up getting shelved and what little plot they had intended was used in a scaled-down fashion in "Something Big". After that, the writers didn't have much use for her and left her in a coma for the remainder of the seriestill the finale where she awakens... just in time todiefor real. Art Evolution: Her second appearance gave more details to her eyes rather than the black dots she had before. This allowed for better expressions. Back for the Finale: She's brought, still unconscious, in the series finale to bring Normal Man and Magic Betty some extra magical power.Then she finally wakes back upa few seconds before exploding. Bad Boss: Sends her familiar to keep Marcie distracted, which resulted in him getting beaten up. When he comes to her, stating he wants to quit after she succeeds in getting Bubblegum's t-shirt, she starts chasing him around her dwelling, blasting him with magic.And she was in a good mood at that point.

characters.name: The Vamps
characters.description: The main antagonists of the "Stakes" mini series. Sometime after the Mushroom Wars they preyed upon the last of the human survivors. Marceline opposed them and killed them all to protect her newfound friends. Though in the process due to her soul sucking powers, gained their abilities as a result after killing them. In the final battle against the king, he bit her and changed her into part vampire to ensure his kind lived on. Accidental Resurrection: The vampiric essence extracted from Marceline using Bubblegum's treatment allows them to resurrect in present-day Ooo to terrorize it once more. Realizing the danger they still possess to the world, Marceline sets out to kill them again before they can regain their full strength. Always Chaotic Evil: Vampires possess a horrible hunger that causes them to crave blood, but this could easily be sated by eating the color red. Instead, vampires hunt humans, and are noted to be unchanging in their ways despite living far longer than the humans they feed on. The soul exceptions areThe Foolwho is simply Chaotic and not Evil, the resurrected Vampire King who realized he had to change, and Marceline who refused to succumb to her hunger. Death by Irony: The vampires devour humans, but eventually end up devoured themselves byMarceline. Divided We Fall: When they were revived, Empress, Hierophant and Moon disagreed with the Vampire King on how to continue their kingdom and went their separate ways.

characters.name: Patience St. Pim
characters.description: A woman from before the Mushroom War who is the newest Ice Elemental. She froze herself before the bombs fell and was unfrozen by Ice King, Finn, and Jake. She wants to be friends with the other elementals (PB, Flame Princess, and Slime Princess) but they don't like her since she had the Ice King kidnap them. Always Someone Better: Justified. She'sfarbetter at wielding ice magic than Ice King due to lacking the insanity issues. Ambiguously Evil: She's trying to make friends with the other elementals andteach them to use their powers, but the lengths she'll go to do such things are quite extreme and her ultimate plans seem uncertain. Be Careful What You Wish For: Patience reached the apex of her power as the Ice Elemental, and (like the others were) is overwhelmed by the emotions associated with her element (despair and ennui), thus literally incapable of enjoying it. Big Bad Ensemble:Of Elements, alongside Betty and Princess Bubblegum, under the virtue of being the reason the elemental princesses get overwhelmed by their powers and wreak havoc on Ooo.

characters.name: Dr. Gross
characters.description: A living, contemporary human from "the island", obsessed with cybernetics and building strange animal hybrids. Ax-Crazy: What would you call aMad Scientistwho has done dozens of twisted experiments and tries to mutilate a child to use him as raw material? Benevolent Boss: When Tiffany becomes her henchman she treats him surprisingly well, giving him a prosthetic arm after his near-death experience of being eaten by the Worm Queen. When Tiffany objects to Dr. Gross killing Finn and Jake as they're his friends, she reassures him that she'll splice him a dog-boy hybrid to be his friend. Even when he turns against her to save them, the worst she threatens him with is a write-up. Cyborg: 60% of her body is advanced prosthetics, with limbs that can telescope and morph into tools and weapons. And it's implied all this was self-inflicted. Dissonant Serenity: She is disturbingly sweet and never loses her composure, even when she is being sadistic.

characters.name: Warren Ampersand
characters.description: A strange monster that Joshua and Margaret encounter during one of their investigations. Abusive Parents:Manages to be even worse than Martin and Hunson combined. Warren has killed hundreds of his own kids, sucking out their life force to prolong his own life. He tries to become aGruesome Grandparentafter Jake reveals the existence of his puppies, but is stopped by Jake throwing him into a black hole. Affably Evil:He’s rather friendly and personable... for a guy who only reproduces so that he can drain his offspring’s lives later on. Aliens Are Bastards: Threatens a pregnant lady,implants its egg into her husband, and chuckles wickedly at the end of it all before going home... it's the embodiment of this trope, albeit one (somewhat) toned down.And then there's the reveal about what he did to his own children. Alien Blood: It bleeds bright green blood after Margaret pricks it with a pin.

characters.name: Mr. M
characters.description: Hugo's mysterious assistant. Call-Back:A few things he says are word for word exactly what something Martin had said earlier in the show, "Here comes the rascal" being one of the most obvious hints as to his identity. Child Hater: He doesn't seem to like children, as seen by remarking"heh, kids right? Always calling out their deadbeat parents." Dramatic Space Drifting:He's last seen drifting off into space. The Faceless: Wears a full-body suit for all of "BMO", though we briefly see his feet,which suggests he's human.

characters.name: Business Men
characters.description: A group of businessmen hired by Finn and Jake in the episode "Business Time." Anti-Villain: Despite eventually becomingTotalitarian Utilitarians, they aren't truly malicious and only do it out of efficiency and protection. Big Bad Slippage: In their debut episode, the businessmen didn't start as antagonists and were more than helpful to Finn and Jake. After an unspecified amount of time taking over the heroic duties while the adventurer duo laze around, they soon becomeTotalitarian Utilitariansin a misguided attempt to protect others. Once Finn fires them, they truly become antagonistic, leading the duo to eventually re-freeze them. Human Popsicle: Finn and Jake found them frozen at the beginning of the episode, and then had them re-freeze after they proved to be a problem. No Name Given: None of their names are spoken, and it's unlikely they can remember them.

characters.name: King Worm
characters.description: A giant worm that absorbs one's life force through their dreams. Body Horror: Nightmares are poisonous for him. When Finn opens his Vault to force him to stop, the Worm King ends up horrifically withered and with flaking and crumbling skin. Early-Bird Cameo: Showed up at the end ofEvictedin the first season before getting his own episode in Season 4. A Glitch in the Matrix: Has the power of putting people in their dreams, but said dreams tend to be very off to keep his target prisoner. Lotus-Eater Machine: Heisone. He tries to put his victims into a nice or normal setting while he sucks their life energy.

characters.name: Penny
characters.description: A little girl who meets Finn and Jake in "City of Thieves". She tells Finn about the King of Thieves, whose chest contains things taken from little girls. It's eventually revealed that she is a thief when she tricks Finn into stealing the King of Thieves's chest, which is full of priceless gems, pearls, and gold. Beneath Suspicion: Finn and Jake never suspect her of being a thief despite living in anOutlaw Townthanks to her outfit, cute appearance, and helpless behavior. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She presents herself as a helpless girl trying to live an honest life in anOutlaw Town, but is a thief herself by tricking Finn and Jake into stealing treasure for her. Even after she's been cleaned up by Finn and Jake, Penny fakes herHeel–Face Turnby "thanking" the former by stealing his clothes in her hug of appreciation before skedaddling. Card-Carrying Villain: "Card CarryingThief", in her own words, after her true colors are revealed.Finn:"But you're just a cute little girl!"Penny:"And,I'm athief!" The Cynic: As seen in the quote above. She sees theOutlaw Townshe lives in as hopeless, where its citizens are incapable ofnotstealing from each other. Not only is she revealed to be a thief herself, but actuallyrevelsin being one.

characters.name: Floradulcina the Witch
characters.description: A witch who curses Jake for stealing a donut from her garden. All There in the Manual: Her name is revealed to be Floradulcina in the tie-in bookAdventure Time: The Enchiridion & Marcy's Super Secret Scrapbook. Canis Latinicus: Floradulcina's spells are a very blatant example of this, which Finnlampshades.Donut Witch:Go back-icus from whence you came-icus!Finn:Aww, now you're just making these up! Confirmed Bachelor: When Jake calls her "Mrs. Witch", she corrects him by telling him she never married. After she curses Jake, he tells her that what she did was an overreaction, giving an example that it's not like he killed her husband, to which she angrily reminds Jake that she's not married. Disproportionate Retribution: She takes away Jake's powers (and also gives him a "chubby man-baby" body) just because he ate one of her countless donuts.

characters.name: The Fear Feaster
characters.description: The manifestation of Finn's fear of the ocean. Big "NO!": He lets one out both times after Finn knocks himself out so his unconscious body can fall into the ocean. The Bus Came Back: He returns in "Billy's Bucket List" after being absent from the series since his debut in Season 1. Jerkass: The Fear Feaster absolutely relishes in taunting Finn over his fear of the ocean. Killed Off for Real: The Grass Sword slays him in "Billy's Bucket List".

characters.name: Demon Cat
characters.description: A demonic cat monster that Finn encounters when exploring a dungeon without Jake. Animalistic Abomination: The Demon Cat, which has a cat-shaped tongue and right limbs that are missing a section connecting to the body. Cats Are Mean: He's a Demon-Cat hybrid with a sadistic attitude, and loves to describe killing Finn in gruesome ways. The Omniscient: Downplayed. He only has an approximate knowledge ofalmosteverything. Our Demons Are Different: He's a hybrid between a demon and a cat.

characters.name: Jelly Cube
characters.description: A blob-like monster that Finn encounters when exploring a dungeon without Jake. Blob Monster: One that is cube-shaped, no less. Gelatinous Encasement: Finn runs into it trying to explore the dungeon. He tries his best to grab the key lodged inside of it, but he does not succeed. Non-Malicious Monster: It's a stationary cube-shapedBlob Monsterwho simply traps whatever prey dumb enough to go inside and seemingly digest them. Shout-Out: It's based on thegelatinous cubemonster fromDungeons & Dragons.

characters.name: Bucket Knight
characters.description: A knight that Finn encounters when exploring a dungeon without Jake. Curb-Stomp Battle: He easily beats Finn with just two punches. David Versus Goliath: The Goliath to Finn's David after he grows bigger. The Bucket Knight then hands Finn's ass quite easily due to his superior size and armored body. Just Toying with Them: Implied. Given his size, the Bucket Knight could've easily killed Finn upon his hits connecting. But he seems to hold back his strength to see if Finn could turn things around. When it becomes clear that Finncan'tdefeat him, the Bucket Knight attempts to go for the killing blow. Miracle-Gro Monster: Bucket Knight originally appears small, but by dousing himself with water, he grows gigantic and gives Finn a major beatdown.

characters.name: Guardian Angel
characters.description: A monster who poses as Finn's guardian angel. Bad Samaritan: The Guardian Angel rescues Finn from the cat monster, heals his wounds, and mends his clothes... then she announces her intention to cook and eat him. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She rescues Finn from the Demon Cat, presenting herself as his guardian angel and restores him back to full health... But is really just a monster in disguise that wants to eat him. Evil Sounds Deep: Her voice becomes much more gravely sounding after showing herNightmare Face. Exact Words: When Finn yells at her to let him go, she bluntly replies "As you wish!" and drops him off into a cage full of broth for her "little kid soup."

characters.name: The Squirrel
characters.description: A red squirrel who first appears in "The Duke", harboring a vendetta against Jake for not printing his letters in his newspaper column "Begs the Question". Ax-Crazy: He becomes increasingly more murderous and unhinged with each subsequent appearance. Disproportionate Retribution: He makes several attempts at Jake's life for no other reason than he never printed his letters in his column. Face–Heel Turn:In "Gumbaldia" he's seen working as a spy for Gumbald. Irrational Hatred: Has an obsessive hatred for Jake so intense that it drives him to violence and eventually complete mental collapse. ...because Jake never prints his letters.

characters.name: Sir Slicer
characters.description: An arrogant knight with impressive armor. Dirty Coward:He flees the fight against GOLB alongside the rest of Gumbald's forces. Jerkass: He spends the entirety of his sole major appearance to mock and belittle Finn for not having cool armor like his. Laser-Guided Karma: Sir Slicer ends up getting payback for following Finn around just to mock him when he ends up embarrassed by falling off his horse and getting a splinter in his finger. Offscreen Teleportation: Somehow, Sir Slicer and his pink horse always manage to get to where Finn is.

characters.name: Tree Witch
characters.description: All Witches Have Cats: At one point, she mentions having a cat who gave birth to kittens. Ass Shove: The Tree Witch threatens to entrap Jake in her "bottomless bottom" if Finn doesn't give her the hair of a princess. Beauty Equals Goodness: Jake is convinced that the Tree Witch is evil because of how ugly she is. He ends up being right. Card-Carrying Villain: She gleefully declares that she'll use her new hair for evil. Jerk with a Heart of Jerk: After being given Finn's hair and seemingly trying to better herself, she declares that she will use her hair for evil.

characters.name: The Piglets
characters.description: Cute Is Evil: The piglets seem adorable and harmless, but they turn out to be the evil. Evil All Along: Despite Finn and Jake's initial assumptions, the piglets are revealed to be evil, using fairy wands to terrorize a mushroom town. I Surrender, Suckers!: Finn is reluctant to kill the last of the piglets because it seems to be surrendering... then the piglet attacks him while his guard is down. Weaksauce Weakness: Ice cream. Making contact with the stuff is enough to make them explode into confetti and flowers.

characters.name: Wendy, Georgy, and Booboo
characters.description: A trio of meanspirited ghosts who help Marceline prank Finn and Jake. The Dividual: The trio are never separated and serve the exact same function with little to differentiate each other. Evil Has a Bad Sense of Humor: The three's idea of a joke is beating Finn and Jake up and tricking them into falling to their death. Go-Karting with Bowser: Finn, Jake, and Marceline are more than happy to watch "Heat Signature" with them shortly after they tried to suck out the guts of the former two. Jerkass: The three of them are relentlessly mean; using Marceline's harmless prank as an excuse to try and kill Finn and Jake for their own amusement.

characters.name: The Cuties
characters.description: Big Little Man: In the episode's climax, the Cuties combine together to create a giant mega-Cutie, shot from a low angle and with intimidating music... but they're still about as tall as Finn's knee. Big, Stupid Doodoo-Head: The Cuties' laughably ineffective attempt to break Finn and Jake by pretending to be their mother's malicious ghost involves them making childish insults. Break the Haughty: After initially boasting about how he and his army will kill Finn and Jake, the Cute King can only cry alongside his army when their failed attack forces him to face the reality that they're not threatening. Combining Mecha: The Cuties combine together in battle, though the result isn't even big enough to reach up to Finn's waist. Cute Is Evil: The Cuties are adorable little creatures that want to be ruthless conquerors, even though they're not particularly good at it.

characters.name: Fight King
characters.description: An evil king and the main antagonist of "Morituri Te Salamus" BFS: He wields one that also functions as aSoul Jar. Blood Knight: An interesting example, he doesn't enjoy fighting as much ashe enjoys watchingotherpeople fight. Covered with Scars: His skin isblackat this point. Didn't Think This Through: Giving Finn theone thingthat could kill him.

characters.name: Ash
characters.description: Marceline's old "Genius Wizard" boyfriend. They started living together in the Tree Fort (before Joshua) until Ash moved Marceline away from the Candy Kingdom to his current house. Then he sold her teddy bear to a witch, earning his girlfriend's anger. Affectionate Nickname: He calls Marceline "Mar-mar". Asshole Victim: In "Betty", Simon lays him out with one hit and steals his flying carpet. It's unethical to do this to someone whom Simon doesn't know whether is good or not, but he deserves it regardless. What makes it funny is that Ash basically got knocked out by Marcie's surrogate father. Doubly funny in "Broke His Crown", when hearing about Ash (not by name) through Marceline made Simon wish he was there to punch him in the face. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing:In his debut, he disguised himself as an old man to trick Finn and Jake into taking Marceline's memory of their break-up.As seen through Marceline's memories in chronological order, Ash seeminglyTook a Level in Jerkassat some point in their relationship. However, going by Marceline's wording ("That's the last straw Ash!") in her memories and her temporary submissive behavior towards him when her memory of their break-up was erased, it's heavily implied that Ash wasalwaysan emotionally abusive boyfriend to her and simply acted nice at times so she doesn't catch on to his true colors. In his debut, he disguised himself as an old man to trick Finn and Jake into taking Marceline's memory of their break-up.

characters.name: Scorcher
characters.description: A serious and dangerous hitman with power over fire. Assassin Outclassin': Ice King attempts to have Scorcher killed by contractinganotherhitman to take him out. Said hitman is almost immediately defeated when Scorcher burns through hisPowered Armor, leaving the small guy inside to run away in fear. The Bus Came Back:Returns in the final season as part of Gumbald's army. Fireball Eyeballs: When he gets mad. Foil: Hyper-competent fire power user to counter Ice King's inept ice magic.

characters.name: Door Lord
characters.description: Anti-Villain: While he's a thief, he's ultimately non-malicious and does so to teach people the value of friendship. Portable Hole: This is the method the Door Lord uses to create doors to other dimensions. Small Role, Big Impact: While a one-off character, him stealing the rock concert shirt Marceline gave Bubblegum is what led them to begin mending their relationship. Thinking Up Portals: As a Door Lord, he has the ability to create doors that lead to anyplace in Ooo that he desires. The Unintelligible: The Door Lord never speaks clearly, only communicating through unintelligible mumbling.

characters.name: The Stag
characters.description: A creepy deer who has been kidnapping the Candy Kingdom citizens and the main antagonist of "No One Can Hear You". Anvil on Head: How it's defeated. Jake unties the bricks attached to his feet, letting them fall onto the Stag's head, caving its skull in. The Cameo: Other than his major appearance in "No One Can Hear You", the Stag also appears in the episode "Sons of Mars", where Magic Man turns him into a telescope. Curb-Stomp Battle: Completely shatters Finn's legs, and leaves him in a coma. In the same fight, it kicks Jake's skull so hard it gives him serious brain damage. The Dog Was the Mastermind: Finn briefly believes it was a delusional Jake who trapped all the candy people. Jake believes it too after he comes to his senses, but then Peppermint Butler reveals everyone was trapped by the Stag who was attacking the candy people earlier in the episode.

characters.name: Hamburger and Hotdog Monster
characters.description: Two giant monsters made of hamburgers and hot dogs that are first encountered by Finn and Jake in Joshua's Dungeon. Anthropomorphic Food: Obviously, they are dungeon monsters made of hamburgers and hot dogs, respectively. A Form You Are Comfortable With: It's heavily implied that they can change into forms depending on who would eventually encounter them. As Finn notes, Jake said he wanted hamburgers, and Finn himself said he wanted hot dogs earlier in the same day. No Name Given: They have no official names.

characters.name: Ugly Monster
characters.description: An ugly monster whom Finn and Jake encounter at the crossroads between his and the Flower Path in Joshua's Dungeon. Gonk: Lampshaded by Jake, as he's "super gross". His body is essentially a large, misshapen green blob composed of many round lumps that are covered with stubbly hair. A large orange-lipped mouth runs vertically down his face; it somewhat resembles Hunson Abadeer's mouth when he is in his monster form, but with rounded teeth. He also sits in a brown puddle of his own slime, which periodically spouts out of the lumps covering his body. It's heavily implied that Joshua has chosen him as a path guardian simply to test whether Finn would correctly judge that the Ugly Monster's path is the safest from the Flower Path. No Name Given: He doesn't have an official name. Punch-Clock Villain: Other than being super gross looking, the Ugly Monster seems to simply be a chill dude whose job is to present the path of least resistance for Finn to take compared to the Flower Path.

characters.name: Fruit Witches
characters.description: A trio of beautiful witches whom Finn and Jake encounter upon the Flower Path in Joshua's Dungeon. They may look peaceful, but are anything but when "partaking of the fruit". Fan Disservice: Despite being scantily-clad humanoid women, they become much more monstrous-looking once they shed their illusions. Forbidden Fruit: The fruits they offer are cursed, and ingesting them will turn the person into a giant flesh fruit for them to feast on. Our Witches Are Different: The Fruit Witches are humanoid monsters who trick any traveler into their part of Joshua's Dungeon into eating their fruit, which will transform them into a flesh fruit so they can devour them through creatures on their heads. Wolf in Sheep's Clothing: They seem calm and pleasant-looking towards Finn and Jake, but accepting their "fruits" will cause them to drop the illusions and reveal them as ugly-looking, carnivorous humanoids.

characters.name: Evil Monster
characters.description: The final monster that Finn and Jake encounter at the end of Joshua's Dungeon. Disney Death: Finn ultimately kills it by stabbing it in the eye and then flinging its gigantic body into a pit. Evil Laugh: It's constantly laughing while tormenting Finn. Laughing Mad: The fact that all it can do is laugh to showcase its evilness. The Speechless: The Evil Monster is only seen laughing with no form of other verbal communication.

characters.name: Princess Monster Wife
characters.description: A grotesque Frankenstein-like being created by Ice King to be his wife with stolen princess parts. Anti-Villain: Justified with great emphasis on theAntipart. Princess Monster Wife is simply a being who is very innocent of the world after her creation and shows great distress over her self-image. The only way she could even be called a "villain" is simply by being made up of the stolen princess parts by Ice King, who treats her as his wife. Body Horror: She's made up of parts of the princesses that Ice King found attractive, which leads to her looking incredibly mismatched. It's enough that anyone other than Ice King would either vomit or faint or both at the sight of her. Body of Bodies: She's an artificial being created by Ice King after he stole parts of various princesses of Ooo and patched them together. Foil: To Betty Grof, as both of them serve as a deep love to their respective spouse. However, whereas Betty was a grown woman who met Simon, Princess Monster Wife was created by Ice King.They also perform aHeroic Sacrifice, with Princess Monster Wife giving back the Princesses' stolen parts and effectively dying, while Betty became the new GOLB to save Simon.

characters.name: Goliad
characters.description: Another of Princess Bubblegum's experiments, Goliad is a candy-Sphinx built to rule the Candy Kingdom past Bubblegum's death. She soon turns out to be impressionable, with a questionable grasp of morals. A God Am I: Not really agod, but the sentiment is there. Ambiguous Innocence: Sure, her endgame is evil, but there doesn't seem to be a smidgen of malice in her. Which only makes her creepier. Body Horror: Her third eye, which seems to unnaturally pop out of her forehead. Cain and Abel: Cain to Stormo's Abel.

characters.name: Samantha
characters.description: An anthropomorphic dog who was imprisoned by Kee-Oth for years for attempting to steal his blood in the past. She was thrown into the same pit where Kee-Oth imprisoned Jake and was forced by the demon to fight to the death. Amazonian Beauty: She's much taller than Jake and is quite the beauty for a warrior. Because Destiny Says So: Her interaction with Jake implies that she's a believer in fate, whether it'll be meeting a potential suitor or an adversary. Best Her to Bed Her: Samantha's challenge to Jake has overtones of this.Samantha:"I don't wait for rescue. I conquer till I am conquered… by love… or by the hand of an adversary." The Bus Came Back:She appeared again in "Gumbaldia" and joined Gumbald's army to attack and conquer the Candy Kingdom.

characters.name: Wyatt
characters.description: One of Tree Trunks' ex-husbands, a miniature manatee with a penchant for being rather whiny and needy. Amicable Exes: A somewhat one-sided one. Even after she divorced him, Wyatt still expresses the desire to get back together with Tree Trunks even when she makes it clear that it will never happen. Be Careful What You Wish For: His appearance in theAdventure Time: Fionna and Cakeepisode "Prismo The Wishmaster" has Wyatt attempting to make a wish to Prismo, but is too annoyed by the alarm sound Prismo's remote keeps making to think clearly. Because of it, Wyatt ends up wishing for quiet and ends up in a new wish reality called Ooofilm in the style of a silent black and white cartoon where he almost gets killed by a train and instantly regrets it while cursing at Prismo. Big Eater: Has tendencies of this, especially when it comes to Tree Trunks' pies. Butt-Monkey: Almost every one of his appearances has him suffer some kind of misfortune.He manages to be this even in the afterlife, where not only is he made to spend eternity in the first dead world tormented by monsters, but becomes its sole resident after Mr. Fox becomes the new Death and allows all the other souls trapped there except Wyatt to ascend to the higher levels.

characters.name: Bella Noche
characters.description: An evil anti-magical being summoned by Bufo, Laser Wizard, and Forest Wizard. He nearly destroys Wizard City before being stopped by Betty. Anti-Magic: A being purely composed of it. Barrier Warrior: He's completely protected by a black cube made ofAnti-Magic, and Ron James' "double negative magic" only makes it grow into a crooked tower. Bilingual Bonus: His name is a mix of "Bella" and "Noche", Spanish for "beautiful" and "night" respectively. Despite being male, the feminine "Bella" is used rather than the masculine "Bello", as the word being described, "Noche", is itself feminine. Bishōnen Line: His regular form is a massive face made out of green slime, while his "true" form is a beautiful, androgynous humanoid.

characters.name: Darren the Ancient Sleeper
characters.description: An ancient being of destruction awakened by Maja in "Something Big". Ancient Evil: He's atleastseveral thousand years old. Attack Its Weak Point: As Eli says, "His weakness is his brain-seed!" Finn kills Darren by stabbing his exposed brain. Blood Knight: In his own words, he only understands destruction, and only fights to the death. Botanical Abomination: He's an ancient, mysterious plant-like being that can tear open portals to other dimensions. It's implied that anyone who is killed by him is erased from all dimensions.

characters.name: Rats
characters.description: As his title implies, he is the King of all rats that live in Finn and Jake's Tree, gnawing at its roots. He is encountered by Kent in his quest to defeat a bad guy. Normally appears as a normal rat with a crown, but can take on the nightmarish form of a Giant Rat Head and cape on top of aSwarm of Rats. Creepy Monotone: A high, but eerily calm and soothing tone... it almost never breaks unless he's attacking or being directly hit. Karma Houdini: Gets away alive but with broken teeth, but stopping his gnawing allows the Tree House to bloom for the first time. Since a rat's teeth can grow back very quickly, it's likely he'll be back. My Species Doth Protest Too Much: A villainous version, all the other Rats in the same episode appear to be nice enough to not fight Kent, and are just protecting the materials needed to make the strongest sword the Blacksmith can make; compare this to his direct hand in draining the Tree House's power by eating away at it. Nothing Is Scarier: Similar to the Lich, Rat King has no funny moments when he appears, and seems to be in a creepy sort of control. His motivation is never explained, and neither are his powers or his origin. There's also the fact that he resides in some sort of otherworldinside ofthe tree and takes the form of a disembodied head on top of a mass of rats.

characters.name: AMO
characters.description: The prototype to BMO, who was designed to receive love rather than give it. All Take and No Give: He was designed toreceivelove, not give it. He expects everyone to obey him and only him. If someone else is given affection, or his orders are ignored, he takes it as a sign that the person offending him doesn't love him and needs to die. Bottomless Magazines: Equipped himself with a weapon that materializes cannonballs out of thin air. Cain and Abel: He's the murderous Cain to BMO's Abel, trying to kill him outright when his trap failed. He also arranged for all of his other MO siblings to go through the same trap which compacted them into a single cube which named All-Mo. Cast as a Mask: Voiced by ChuckMcCannwhen pretending to be Moe, and Thu Tran when he drops the disguise.

characters.name: Bandit Princess
characters.description: A ruthless thief who kills people and steals their gold. Bad People Abuse Animals: She kills Box Prince. The Bus Came Back:Returns as part of Gumbald's army. The Corrupter:It's implied that she was one of the reasons why Fern became evil after the time he spent with her as Finn Sword. Freudian Excuse:Parodied. According to her, the reason why she became a bandit is because she was born with rabies and her parents never loved her.

characters.name: In General
characters.description: Adaptational Mundanity: Rather than fantasy creatures and magic, the world is a recreation of 21st-century Earth, though not without some minor idiosyncrasies. Nonhuman or humanoid characters from the fanfic universe have been turned into humans here. Adapted Out: Some characters don't have human or animal counterparts: BMO cameos as a nonsapient alarm clock, and many of the less important Candy Kingdom citizens only appear as part of Gary's edible candymenschen project. Alternate Universe: Notable in that it's an alternate take on Fionna and Cake's universe rather than the original, where the characters are normal humans and animals in a present-day setting, similar to aModern AU Fic.This is because, due to being placed in Ice King's mind, Fionna and Cake's version of Ooo was stripped of its fantastical elements when Ice King was stripped of his magic and madness and returned to being Simon Petrikov. Brought Down to Normal: All the inhabitants of this world lost their magical abilities. City Planet: Minimized.The season 2 finale reveals that Fionna's city is the only settlement on Earth. It's implied that this is a side effect of her world being canonized inThe Multiverse.

characters.name: Joshua and Margaret
characters.description: Jake's parents, who also adopted Finn after finding him in a forest. Their job is to hunt monsters around Ooo. Abusive Parents: Joshua is adownplayedexample. In the prerecorded messages he left for Finn and Jake in his dungeon, he hurls insults at Finn and convinces Jake to do so as well. The harsh words that promptly come from both his brother and father (the latter of whom Finn hasn't seen in years due to Joshua's death)nearly causes Finn to kill himself. However, it's clear that Joshua just misjudged how hurtful his words would be to Finn, ashe only said those things as a method ofTough Loverather than out of malice. In his final message,he tells Finn that he loves him and that he knows he'll do great things. Action Dad: Joshua's no less of a badass after becoming a father. He even built anentiredungeon filled with the most dangerous creatures he could captureall on his ownas a sacred rite for his adopted son, Finn, to inherit the Demon Blood Sword. Action Girl: Margaret, who forms half of Joshua and Margaret Investigations, definitely qualifies. She seems to favor a crossbow and shuriken. Action Mom: Even after becoming a mother to three kids doesn't dull Margaret's fighting skills, but she's seldom seen fighting.

characters.name: Jermaine
characters.description: Finn and Jake's third brother. He appears early on in flashbacks, but doesn't appear in person until "Jermaine". Aloof Big Brother: Well, he's not their big brother, but Jermaine acts like it, preferring to do his own thing. He loves Finn and Jake, but he doesn't get their childlike behavior, so he spends most of his time painting. Badass Normal: Despite not having powers, he holds his own when it comes to dealing with demons. Big Little Brother:Justifiedand then subverted as they grew older. "Joshua and Margaret's Investigations" shows that Jermaine is much bigger than his older half-brother, Jake, as an infant. The reason why Jake is smaller is due to being born from Joshua'shead, which Jake's biological parent impregnates Joshua by biting him. Big Ol' Eyebrows: Pretty much the only thing that makes him visually distinct from Jake.

characters.name: Jake Jr.
characters.description: One of Jake and Lady Rainicorn's puppies, who inherited Jake's mischievous side. She's the second oldest of the Pups. Eyeless Face: Unlike the other pups, she doesn't have visible eyes or a nose. She does have several wrinkles on her face, but exactly what they are or why her face is like this is unclear. She also has an unusual mouth which appears to open both horizontally and vertically, and her horn is on her lower back.Turns out her odd face may be inherited from her extra-dimensional "grandfather". Gender-Blender Name: She's a girl named Jake. In the Blood: She has recently become a thief like her father was in his youth. Prehensile Hair: Her hair can grow and be controlled in the same way her father controls his body.

characters.name: T.V.
characters.description: Another of Jake and Lady's puppies. He still lives with his mother. He's the third oldest of the Pups. Basement Dweller: Lives with his mother and spends his time playing video games. Cannot Tell Fiction from Reality: He hallucinates that the events in BP's diary are happening to him. Jake notes that he was always susceptible to fantasy. Defective Detective:He becomes a detective at the end of the series. His very powerful imagination and ability to identify with people could theoretically prove to be assets. Geek Physiques: He's the chubbiest of his siblings.

characters.name: Kim Kil Whan
characters.description: The most responsible of Jake and Lady's puppies. He's also the youngest of the Pups. Aloof Big Brother: Inverted. To his less responsible, older siblings. Beard of Evil: Though he's more amoral than evil, he has a classic pointy villain beard. Corrupt Corporate Executive: He buys out his father's treehouse and splits it into thirty-seven tiny apartments that he rents out. Subverted in that this is an effort to get his Dad to get a job and learn responsibility. Doesn't Know Their Own Child:Inverted. While Kim Kil Whan isn't wrong about Jake's carefree lifestyle, he never knew that his fatheriscapable of being a responsibleParental Substitutetowards his uncle long before he was born.

characters.name: Viola
characters.description: Another of Jake and Lady's puppies. She's the fourth youngest of the Pups. Beleaguered Assistant: She ends up becoming one to LSP in "Summer Showers", even though she desperately wants the lead role in LSP's upcoming play. LSP acts like aPrima Donna Directorthroughout the episode and constantly pushes Viola around until Violafinally has enough. Daddy's Girl: Thinks Jake is the best father in the world, despite hardly ever seeing him, and is the only one of Jake's kids who respects him afterRapid Aging. The Dog Bites Back: At LSP in "Summer Showers", who makes Viola her personal assistant for her upcoming play and constantly pushes her around. She finally has enough after LSP decides to cast herself in the lead role (despite Viola already knowing the part by heart), teleporting LSP away so she can take part in the show. Flowers of Femininity: She wears a large blue flower on her head, emphasizing how feminine she is compared to her more tomboyish sisters.

characters.name: Charlie
characters.description: The last of Jake and Lady's puppies. She's the oldest of the Pups. Brilliant, but Lazy: She knows she could be good at Card Wars, but she's not into it. Cool House: Lives in a pre-Mushroom War Egyptian pyramid that's located halfway across the planet from Ooo. Exact Words: She agrees to play a game of Card Wars with Jake in exchange for one of his bones. They easily win the first round at the Card Wars tournament, but she quits right after that. In her words, "One bone, one game". Fortune Teller: Her main interests are mysticism, spirituality, and cartomancy.

characters.name: Bronwyn
characters.description: Kim Kil Whan's daughter and, thus, Jake's granddaughter. Bratty Teenage Daughter: Would rather go skateboarding than focus on her schoolwork. Heinz Hybrid: Has a dog, rainicorn, bearandEldritch Abominationin her ancestry. Kid Sidekick:"Obsidian" reveals that she's now going on adventures with Finn years after "Come Along With Me". Despite this, she hasn't aged a bit since her last appearance. Non-Human Humanoid Hybrid: Where tobegin?She is half bear from her mother's side while Kim is of course, half rainicorn from Lady and half dog from Jake whileJake himself is technically half dog and half extradimensional creature, thus, all of his kids would be one quarter dog and one quarter alien being, thus Bronwyn is half bear, quarter rainicorn, 1/8th dog and 1/8th alien

characters.name: Mr. Pig
characters.description: A pig who used to eat people for the mob. Now married to Tree Trunks. Apologetic Attacker: "Uh, I'm sorry y'all. They're making me do this. I'll try to make it quick." Cannot Spit It Out: He has some trouble admitting his love to Tree Trunks. Fed to Pigs: His job was to be one of these pigs, until Finn and Jake rescued him. Good Parents: To Sweet P. Whether this will actually do any good remains to be seen.Well Sweet P does become ahero in his own right.

characters.name: Shelby
characters.description: Shelby is a talking worm who lives in Jake's viola. Accidental Misnaming: He objects to being called "Shelby the worm who lives in Jake's viola".Shelby: You can just call me Shelby. Artistic License – Religion: Despite priests vowing to celibacy, Shelby has a girlfriend. Catchphrase: After learning the phrase from Jake's abuse of it for the sake of comedy in "Video Makers", Shelby adopts "Check, Please!" as one which also ends up being his final line in "Come Along With Me". Creator Cameo: He's voiced by Pendleton Ward.

characters.name: Kent
characters.description: Shelby's little brother (actually a piece of his tail-end that got cut off performing "parkour" and landing on some string at a party). Kent quickly learned to talk, grow appendages, and after Shelby gets advice on brothers from Jake, Go and beat bad guys, which begins his first adventure into the tree itself. Chaste Hero: Due to being born literally a few minutes earlier, when the Rat Knight gives him a choice of love or the magic earth he has, Kent picks the earth without a second thought. Does This Remind You of Anything?: The party that led to his creation in the first place, along with the fact that Shelby passes out and wakes up from said party not remembering what happened. Expy: He shares many Similarities withKirby, both are small, round, pink, baby-like characters that go on an adventure blissfully to defeat a nightmarish villain. Maybe Magic, Maybe Mundane: Kent just sort of comes into being, and its unknown whether or not this just happens with a worms body pieces being cut, or if there was some outside influence behind his.

characters.name: Susan Strong
characters.description: A member of an underground-dwelling group of humans. The "humans" she lives with are eventually revealed to behyoo-mans, a strange race ofFish Peopleliving in the ruins of human civilization. Susan herself is the only true human amongst them. She gets a focus arc in season 8 explaining her origins.Her real name is Kara, and she was an elite member of humanity's "Seeker" caste who was sent to Ooo 16 years ago to find Martin and baby Finn and bring them home, but somehow ended up getting lost herself. Ambiguously Gay: She has an extremely close relationship with Frieda in the Islands mini-series. Ambiguously Human: Initially, she was introduced as a member of the Hyoo-mans, but was not confirmed to be one of them. She is later revealed to be fully human, though she does have some cybernetic implants from her home. Connected All Along:Not only is Susan the one who introduced Finn's parents to each other, but she is the Seeker tasked with finding Martin and Finn when they disappear, which eventually leads her to become amnesiac. Cowardly Lion: Better than the rest of her people, certainly.

characters.name: NEPTR
characters.description: NEPTR (or Never Ending Pie Throwing Robot), pronounced "Nepter", is a robot that throws never ending pies. Created by Finn to get back at Jake for being pranked. Androids Are People, Too: He is usually ignored most of the time by Finn, Ice King, Jake and BMO but he has proven to be sapient to the point that in the alternate Farmworld timeline he has a human counterpart, which implies that he possesses a soul. Ambiguously Evil: For a moment, when Ice King infused him with his private particles he also inherited some of his evil, saying he made his pies with boisenberry and poison, and expressing an interest in kidnapping princesses. He settles on good once he chooses Ice King... to prank with a pie to the face. Artificial Family Member: He is considered a son by both Finn and the Ice King. He is later accepted as a stepson by Huntress Wizard. Ascended Extra: He went from a one-off character in "What is Life", to a recurring companion for BMO from "Hot to the Touch" onward. Starting with "Sad Face", his appearances throughout the series increased even further.

characters.name: Billy
characters.description: A legendary hero and Finn and Jake's idol. He battled hundreds of famous villains, such as the Lich and the Fire Count (also a bear), but eventually believed that it was a waste of time, as new villains would rise up. He later took up a philosophy of nonviolent community activism, but returned to the hero fold after Finn convinced him that saving lives was worth it. Actual Pacifist: In "His Hero", Billy claims to be this because he thinks using violence against evil is pointless and this is because more evil pops up. Ambiguous Situation: Original storyboards state that Billy imprisoned Martin for crimes he was innocent of. While this has since been changed so that Martin was more than likelycompletelyguilty of any crimes he committed, the fact that Billy inexplicably knows Martin and where he is may imply that he still have been the one to put him away. Arch-Enemy: The Lich, it seems, as well as the Fire Count, who was to Billy what the Ice King is to Finn. Badass Normal: He has no powers or magical abilities to speak of, but he was such a badass he beat and sealed the Lich for anywhere from decades to centuries.

characters.name: Tiffany Oiler
