Considering what Prismo can already do and given what it might take to piss Prismo's boss off, that says a frightening amount about how powerful they must be.Prismo:Now if that happens, my boss-let me repeat that,MY. BOSS.will holdmeresponsible.And by proxy, we are all in hot water. Prismo also cannot recover beings that have been erased or assimilated byGOLB. Furthermore, in "Prismo the Wishmaster", it is revealed that he cannot directly interfere in realities affected by the power ofGOLBsuch as Fionna's world. Ambiguously Gay: Prismo's pink-colored, he talks with a slight lisp, and he tends to chill in a hot tub with his guy-friends Jake and the Cosmic Owl. One topic of discussion in his room is him finding a girlfriend, which he awkwardly hems and haws over. He is also overjoyed when Jake casually claims he loves him and is very clearly deeply attached to Jake, d

characters.name: Cosmic Owl
characters.description: A mysterious and important entity in the land of Ooo, it appears to others in visions. It speaks in a Southern drawlinitiallyand is a friend of Prismo. Alien Blood: His blood is golden and sparkling, like he is. Animalistic Abomination: A golden energy owl that appears in others' consciousnesses and, according to the Why-Wolves, is capable of devouring entire populations if they prove too numerous. An origin story flashback reveals he was originally more humanoid-looking, but was transformed into an owl-like appearanceas part of his punishment for eating a forbidden pizza and betraying his conjoined twin brother. Back from the Dead:In the second season ofFionna and Cake, he's killed by Huntress Wizard, but ends up brought back to life a few episodes later by his brother, the Karmic Worm. Big Damn Heroes:Pops up in the final episode disguised as a singing poodle to interrupt PB and Gumbald's dream-battle.

characters.name: Abraham Lincoln
characters.description: Balancing Death's Books:He accidentally executed Jake thinking he was the Magic Man. He travels to the Eighth Dead World to bring him back, where he meets with Death. When Death refuses the payment of one penny, the King offers his immortality instead, killing him and turning him to stone (an exact replica of the Lincoln Memorial, in fact). Early-Bird Cameo: Lincoln appeared as early as the2006 shortin a very... weird scene, and never came back until "Son of Mars" in 2012! Friendless Background: As revealed in "Sons of Mars":Lincoln: "My judgement was less than the standard by which I judge my peers... of which I have none." God-Emperor: He's the Martian King. He also appears to be a god. Heroic Sacrifice:In order to bring Jake back from the dead, he offers Death his own immortality.

characters.name: Grob Gob Glob Grod
characters.description: A four-faced deity from Mars, and Magic Man's older brother. Baldness Angst: The weird geometric headgear is to hide the fact that Magic Man used his magic to make him bald. Cain and Abel: The Abel to Magic Man's Cain. Cosmic Entity: But like the Cosmic Owl, the extent of his power isn't clear. Flaming Sword: His weapon of choice, which he used to defeat Orgalog.

characters.name: Death
characters.description: Ruler of the Land of the Dead, Death has power over the deceased and is able to raise them whenever he wills it. Best friends with Peppermint Butler. Affably Evil: Despite being an overall nice guy, "The Gift That Reaps Giving" hints that Death will not back down from doing despicable things if it gets him what he wants. In that short, he wants to gift a mixtape to his girlfriend, and decides that the easiest way to acquire one is by murdering an innocent child who has it. Cooldown Hug:He appears to try one of these on his son, New Death, when the latter begins arguing with Death's attempts to bond with him over gardening. It would've worked if it wasn't for the Lich's machinations. Deal with the Devil: In "Sons of Mars", Death agrees to resurrectJakein exchange forAbraham Lincoln's immortality.It's also implied that he once revived someone for Lincoln in exchange for apenny. The Death of Death:New Death, his son, murders him while under the Lich's influence.

characters.name: Life
characters.description: The personification of life. Death's girlfriend. Appears in the digital shorts "The Gift That Reaps Giving" and "Frog Seasons: Winter". Abusive Parents: She admits she has no love for her family, and that all she cares for is her job. This, despite having a son. Berserk Button: Attempting to impede her job will enrage her in such a way that she'll do everything to helpkillthe one responsible, even if that person isher own son. Bewitched Amphibians: An odd example - the "Frog Seasons: Winter" short hasthe frog Finn and Jake have been following turns into Life after putting on its crown. Bilingual Bonus: After finding out inTogether Againthat New Death has stopped the cycle of reincarnation, she furiously mutters in French as she assembles the Kiss of Life, the artifact meant to stop him. Doubles as a bit ofGenius Bonus, as she was in a loving relationship with Death...and French is often called "the language of love".Life: HE DIDWHAT?!He's willing to snatch my entire purpose from ME?!Après tout ce que j'ai fais pour ce garçon, après tout ce que j'ai fais pour lui. Non mais c'est pas possible, ce n'est pas possible. Non ça me... ça m'infurie complètement! Mais c'est pas possible!(Translation:"After all I did for that boy! After everything I did for him! No, but it's not possible! That's not possible! No, I'm... I'm completely infuriated! But that's not possible!")

characters.name: Catalyst Comet
characters.description: The otherworldly force that causes major and often dangerous changes in the world whenever it passes. In "The Comet" it is revealed to besentient and actually rather benevolent. Alien Geometry: It's reallya hollowed-out sphere with 3 eyes. Arc Villain: Sorta one for season 6.Subverted when it's revealed to not really be evil. Ascended to a Higher Plane of Existence: Its offer to Finn, which he declines.Martin is eager to take it up, though. Comet of Doom: Causes catastrophic events whenever it passes.It turns out that it isn't a malevolent force, but rather just an agent of change.

characters.name: Wishy
characters.description: A magical entity living in a crayon-like dimension who grants wishes to those who seek him out. Always a Bigger Fish: He seems to share Prismo's limitations regarding the limits of wish magic, such as not being able to interfere with the actions of a higher entity. His attempt to cure Finn of the Heart of the Forest's essence only results in Finnaging prematurely. Equivalent Exchange: His wish-granting costs a piece of the wisher's soul. He doesn't mention this, so it's not exactly aDeal with the Devil. Flashy Teleportation: In episode "Blenanas", he teleport Finn and the Ice King to BLE Magazine's offices. Sugar Bowl: We don't see much of his dimension, but given that what we do see consists largely of clouds and rainbows and looks as though it was drawn by a child, it can be said to fit this. The only thing casting doubt on this is that the Ice King requires a demonic wishing eye to get there.

characters.name: Kheirosiphon
characters.description: A cosmic entity formerly tasked with guarding sacred flames only to abandon his post to become a teahouse owner and is later hunted down by Scarab for it. Dangerous Deserter: Is classified as being this in Scarab's criminal database despite just wanting to live out his days serving tea to customers. Earn Your Happy Ending:In the epilogue ofFionna and Cakehe finds work as a waiter at the bakery in Fionna's world after escaping imprisonment and the battle with Scarab is over. Elemental Personalities: A fiery being with an equally fiery personality once he drops his mortal disguise. Happy Ending Override:In the second season however, he's fired from his job and gets another one — as Queenie'senforcer. Thankfully, by the end of the season he's back to his happy ending by way of opening a tea stand at the new Sweet Spot.

characters.name: Orbo
characters.description: A high-ranked cosmic entity and judge for those who commit cosmic crimes. Beware the Nice Ones: He'srather affablebut even Scarab knows better than to tick him off.Orbo:Nice speech.Say goodbye to your legs. The Dragon: Seems to be this for theTop God. Flashy Teleportation: Orbo has the ability to teleport specific individuals from anywhere inThe Multiverseto his presence and send them in turn to any location he knows in bursts of light. Pointy-Haired Boss: He completely ignores Scarab's report that Prismo has created an unauthorized universe becausehe thinks Prismo is cool. He evenphysically threatensScarab for refusing to drop the matter. In Orbo's defence, Prismo is normally very good at his job as Wishmaster and is going through an emotional low.

characters.name: "The Boss"
characters.description: The highest-ranking entity in the cosmic chain of command. Always a Bigger Fish: In the episode "Cheers",GOLBettycanonizes Fionna's world without problems, which implies that she is at the same level or higher in the hierarchy of the Boss of the other cosmic entities of the multiverse. The Dreaded: Is so powerful that no other high-level being wants to draw their ire lest they receive horrible punishments for it. Even More Omnipotent: They're not Prismo's boss without a much higher degree of omnipotence, and nearly every deity and cosmic being answers to them.Prismo:Now if that happens, my boss-let me repeat that,MY. BOSS.will holdmeresponsible.And by proxy, we are all in hot water. The Ghost: They've been mentioned multiple times but have yet to make an onscreen appearance.

characters.name: The Heart of the Forest
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Personification: It is the physical avatar of an extradimensional tree linked to the plant life of the multiverse. Captured Super-Entity: The Heart of the Forest of Ooo that the Green Wizards use for their power is revealed to be a partially buried creature that's chained to the spot. De-power: When the Huntress Wizard accidentally injured it, it decided to eliminate the stolen magic of the Green Wizards. Face Death with Dignity: Subverted. The Heart of The Forest from Fionna’s world is willing to let itself killed by Huntress Wizard, but the latter refuses to kill it even if it means not being able to get the cure to save Finn, and instead she bows to it in penance. It repays her change of heart by giving her its blessing. God in Human Form: It has avatars of himself throughout the multiverse.

characters.name: Y5
characters.description: A young teen scientist who lives on The Drift. Beware the Nice Ones: She finally snaps near the end. Calling the Old Man OutAfter spending so long pining for her parents' approval, she eventually calls them out for never listening to her before going off to save BMO and expose Hugo's schemes. Character Development: She starts out as someone who simply does as she's told and afraid to speak her mind, but her bonding with BMO helped her grow into a more heroic and confident person. Deuteragonist: Of "BMO".

characters.name: Olive
characters.description: A silent shapeshifting service droid that acts as BMO's sidekick when he ends up on The Drift. Meaningful Name: Olive is green, has an antenna and has a red pupil, loosely resembling a pitted, pimento olive with a toothpick. The Speechless: It never speaks, and presumably can't due to lacking a mouth.

characters.name: CGO
characters.description: A small robot that works in The Drift's garbage pod. Mr. Exposition: She's the one to tell Y5 about Hugo's backstory. Poor Communication Kills: She knew all along about Hugo's true nature, but nobody bothered to talk to her (or if they did,didn't believe her) because she was just a lowly garbage-sorting robot. Shoddy Knockoff Product: She admits that she's basically a bootleg MO.

characters.name: Space Moth
characters.description: Ascended to a Higher Plane of Existence:Alongside Martin in "The Comet". Big Creepy-Crawlies: It can easily fit Martin and Finn in its mouth. Non-Mammal Mammaries: Somehow, despite being a moth, it provides milk.

characters.name: Martin  2
characters.description: Morality Pet: Averted. While Martin seems fond of him, even giving him a nickname, he leaves Martin 2 high and dry when it turns out he was the one the guards were after the whole time. Older Than They Look: He turns out to be an old man, which we don't find out until aGross-Up Close-Upof him. Pint-Size Powerhouse: He is able to hold his own against several guards many times his size.

characters.name: Finn Mertens
characters.description: Finn's counterpart in the Farmworld universe. A Tragedy of Impulsiveness: His attempt to solve his family's money problems by stealing the ice crown triggered a series of events that only made him an outcast to the rest of his world. Accidental Murder: The explosion turned Marceline into a skeleton and a frightened Finn kicked her skull into the remains of the Lich's essence. Alcoholic Parent: According to Jay, his father told him about the ice crown when he drank too much cider. All for Nothing: The state of Farmworld after everything Finn went through after being freed from the Ice Crown's curse, so that all his actions to try to help his family were in vain. Back in "Finn The Human", Finn Mertens was the son of a farmer whose family was constantly tormented by the Destiny Gang. Now, 14 years later, he is... a farmer whose family is continuously tormented by the Destiny Gang. Finn went through hell to end up right back where he started, only now he is traumatized by his time as The Snowman and grieving the death of the mother of his children.

characters.name: Jake
characters.description: Jake's counterpart in the Farmworld universe. Alternate Species Counterpart: Because the Mushroom Bomb didn't go off, the lack of magic in the world resulted in Jake being an ordinary non-sapient dog. Demonic Possession: Farmworld Jake ends up possessed by the Lich. Fortunately, both Finn the Human and Farmworld Finn would purge the Lich from his body and restore him to being a normal dog. In Spite of a Nail: Despite the lack of magic in the Farmworld universe, Jake ends up being entangled in shapeshifting magic regardless. Unfortunately for him, it's because he gets possessed by the Lich. Richard Nixon, the Used Car Salesman: As an ordinary non-sapient dog, Jake isn't an adventurer like his prime timeline counterpart.

characters.name: Marceline Abadeer
characters.description: Marceline's counterpart in the Farmworld universe. Age Without Youth: She lived for a thousand years protecting Simon's corpse from looters, but without her vampire powers keeping her youthful, she became a very elderly woman. Cool Old Lady: Though she is pretty batty. Dead Alternate Counterpart: To the main timeline Marceline in the events of "Jake the Dog", as Farmworld Marceline dies from beingStripped to the Bonefrom being submerged in the mutagen waste of the Mushroom Bomb. Distaff Counterpart: To the Ice King, with Simon's early death and her never getting bitten, she grew up to be an insane old hermit just like him, with a body type resembling how he looks with his robe.

characters.name: Simon Petrikov
characters.description: Simon's counterpart in the Farmworld universe. Crown of Power: Combined withArtifact DominationandSentient Phlebotinum, his magical crown grants the power to create and manipulate ice and snow, but gradually consumes the wearer's sanity, which varies according to its use and willpower. Dead Alternate Counterpart: This Simon died in aHeroic Sacrificeto stop the Mushroom Bomb, as opposed to the Simon from the timelines that lead to the creation of Ooo and Simon's transformation into the Ice King. Heroic Sacrifice: He was able to stop the bomb that would create the Lich, but in doing so, was crushed underneath the frozen bomb. Major Injury Underreaction: His only reaction to being crushed by a massive, frozen nuclear bomb is "Little help?"

characters.name: Choose Bruce
characters.description: Choose Goose's counterpart in the Farmworld universe. Alternate Species Counterpart: A human version of Choose Goose. Con Man: By the time ofFionna and Cakewith the brutal rule of the Destiny Gang, he's resorted to conning suckers out of their valuables. Mugging the Monster:He threatens Fionna with a spiked club when she tries to get her phone back, and Cake wallops him with a shapeshifted fist for his trouble.He later tries to extort a disguised Scarab out of any valuables he has in exchange for information regarding Fionna, Cake, and Simon's whereabouts. Scarab's response reveals his true face and threatens to kill Choose Bruce unless he talks.Scarab:You there. Have you seen a group of travelers recently?(smiles)Strangeones?Choose Bruce:(cockily)I might feel smarter, if you had something to barter!Scarab:I offer you(smile widens)your unmurdered life.(reveals his real face)RAGHHHH!!Choose Bruce:(freaked out)M-m-man, cat, and woman followed Jay Mertens west! I… hope that answers your request… He threatens Fionna with a spiked club when she tries to get her phone back, and Cake wallops him with a shapeshifted fist for his trouble.

characters.name: Bobby
characters.description: Billy's counterpart in the Farmworld universe. Alternate Species Counterpart: A human version of Billy. Badass in Distress: Given who his counterpart is, his being introduced as a captive of Farmworld Finn and the Lich serves to establish their threat.

characters.name: Little Destiny
characters.description: The daughter of Big Destiny and a member of the Destiny Gang. '80s Hair: There's a reason Cake refers to her as "Mullet Girl". Dating What Daddy Hates: Big D does not take finding out Little D is high-fiving Jay with her mouth very well. Hidden Depths:Her contribution to the talent show in "The Insect That Sang" shows she's actually quite a talented knife thrower. I Choose to Stay:After being delivered to Fionna's world to help stop the Scarab, she and Jay ultimately choose to stay in it.

characters.name: Peanut
characters.description: The son of Big Destiny and a member of the Destiny Gang. The Dog Bites Back:After beingThe Un-Favoriteand enduring Big Destiny's abuse for presumably his whole life, Peanut snaps and murders him. Patricide:He murders his father in "The Lion of Embers. The Un-Favorite: Big Destiny thinks very little of Peanut, especially when compared to Little Destiny.Even when Peanut reveals to him that Little Destiny and Jay are dating, Big Destiny completely disregards him and kicks him down into the crater with them. "Well Done, Son" Guy: Peanut is shown to be desperate for Big Destiny's approval. Unfortunately for him, he far prefers his sister.

characters.name: Farmworld Finn's wife
characters.description: The deceased wife of Farmworld Finn and the mother of Jay, Bonnie, and the other Mertens children. Action Mom: Implied. Given how much of aCrapsack Worldshe lives in after the Destiny Gang took over, she's implied to possess a good amount of fighting skills to defend herself and her family, especially whenit's confirmed that she's the Farmworld's version of Huntress Wizard. Alternate Species Counterpart:She's the human counterpart to Huntress Wizard. Badass Cape: Implied to have worn a cape as part of her everyday attire,given that she's the Farmworld's version of Huntress Wizard and one of her kids quickly mistakes Huntress Wizard as her when HW grows a body. Dead Alternate Counterpart: Impliedand confirmed to be theAlternate Selfof Huntress Wizard, and she's long dead by the start ofFionna and Cake.

characters.name: Jay Mertens
characters.description: Finn's son in the Farmworld universe. Continuity Nod: Like his previous son in the Pillow Universe, he is named Jay. I Choose to Stay:After being delivered to Fionna's world to help stop the Scarab, he and Little Destiny ultimately choose to stay in it. Star-Crossed Lovers: He is secretly dating Little Destiny, the daughter of Big Destiny, the crime boss whose gang is harassing his family.

characters.name: Bonnie Mertens
characters.description: Finn's daughter in the Farmworld universe. The Cameo: She only makes a cameo appearance in "The Bear and The Rose", the last episode of Season 2. Cheerful Child: She's always upbeat and full of wonder about everything, in sharp contrast to the rather miserable universe she lives in. Continuity Nod: Like his previous daughter in the Pillow Universe, she is named Bonnie. Tagalong Kid: Averted. She tries to be one when Jay is taking Fionna, Cake, and Simon to where the crown is hidden, but Jay stuffs her in the hay so she can't follow them or tattle.

characters.name: Other Mertens Kids
characters.description: Adaptation Species Change: One was a robot, and the other was a griffin. Children Are Innocent: Implied,as one of them believes that their mother had "come back" (when it was really Huntress Wizard) despite being dead. Continuity Nod: One of them looks like a human version of Stormo, and the other of NEPTR, both of whom are considered, by some metric, to be Finn's "son". Doppelgänger Gets Same Sentiment: Finn's Farmworld kids reacted to Huntress Wizard's apparent death as if she were their own mother. Harmful to Minors: The sudden death of Huntress Wizard in Farmworld leaves the versions of her children visibly traumatized.

characters.name: Quilton
characters.description: The Pillow People leader. Eyes Always Shut: Quilton, the Pillow People leader and Finn's father-in-law, always has at least one eye shut.

characters.name: Roselinen
characters.description: The daughter of Quilton, the mayor of Pillow World. Girl of the Week: She married Finn and even had children with him, but was soon left behind at the episode's end. However, due to the events of “Puhoy” possibly beingAll Just a Dream, it's unknown whether it's real or not.

characters.name: Jay and Bonnie
characters.description: Finn's Kids in the Pillow World. Dead Guy Junior: Lost rather than dead, but it's implied that Finn named them after Jake and Bonnibel (PB's rarely-used personal name.) Half-Human Hybrid: They are Finn’s human-pillow children. Identical Granddaughter: In retrospect, an adult Bonnie looks like a less blonde, pink-skinned version of her paternal grandmother, Minerva Campbell. Strong Family Resemblance:Jay, as a teenager, seemed to greatly resemble Finn, in both physical appearance and clothing. He wore a blue shirt and a backpack that was two shades of green. He also had a small dagger on the right side of his waist that looked like a miniature version of Finn's Demon Sword.As an adult, Bonnie is a dead-ringer for her paternal grandmother, Minvera Campbell, in retrospect.

characters.name: Weirdo Finn
characters.description: Alternate Species Counterpart: This version of Finn is a creature with rabbit-like characteristics instead of a human.

characters.name: Flower Marcy
characters.description: Alternate Species Counterpart: This version of Marceline is aPlant Personinstead of a vampire.

characters.name: The Winter King
characters.description: An alternate sane and handsome version of the Ice King, who's a beloved leader terrorized by the deranged Candy Queen. Affably Evil:He turns out to be a far more sociopathic version of the Ice King without the madness caused by the magic crown, but is genuinely aNice Guydespite his callous behavior towards the Candy Queen. Alas, Poor Villain:Despite his questionable actions, it is understood that the loss of the people he cared about was what wore down what remained of his morality. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: He's the Ice King if he were smart, handsome, and retained his sanity that the Crown took away, using his powers for good and opposing an insane evil version of PB.However, he once was like the main universe Ice King and managed to make himself into the "awesome" version by cursing PB to be driven to insanity by transferring the Crown's madness to her without the princess' consent. Asshole Victim:His death is... unpleasant, to put it mildly, but it's hardly as if he didn't deserve it given what he did.

characters.name: Ice Scouts
characters.description: Two beings made of ice by the Winter King. They serve as his assistants and bodyguards. I'm Melting!:After Winter King's death, the ice magic that gave them life is no longer in effect. This causes the Ice Scouts to melt into puddles of water. Praetorian Guard: They serve as Winter King's bodyguards and would repeatedly rescue him from being kidnapped by the Candy Queenmanytimes during an entire century. Shout-Out: To the Pearls fromSteven Universe.

characters.name: Marceline
characters.description: The Winter World's version of Marceline the Vampire Queen. The Cameo: She's only shown in Winter King's visual drawing in his song. Killed Offscreen: Given the appearance ofIce Marceline, it's a sign that Winter World Marceline perished off-screen. Morality Pet: Like her prime counterpart, she served as this to her world's version of Simon/Ice King.Her death ends up contributing to the creation of theWinter King. Posthumous Character: She's long dead by the time of the episode.

characters.name: Ice Marceline
characters.description: An ice replica of Marceline who was created by the Winter King. The Cameo: She's only shown in Winter King's castle as Cake explores the Winter Kingdom. Gilded Cage: The brief appearance of Ice Marceline showed her happily imprisoned in her own roomdue to the Winter King wishing to keep her safe at all costs. Killed Offscreen:After the Winter King dies, she's reduced to a puddle off-screen due to the ice magic no longer keeping her animated. Replacement Goldfish: For the Winter King after the death of the Winter World's version of Marceline.

characters.name: Betty
characters.description: This world's version of Betty. Killed Offscreen:If the Winter King is to be believed, she died over a thousand years ago. Posthumous Character: She's long dead by the time of the episode. Small Role, Big Impact: Similarly to Marceline, she gets very little mention other than the Winter King not remembering her as anything other than "the dead one" when Simon brings her up. This ends up being a big indicator thatthe Winter King is more Ice King than he is Simon. Her death very likely also contributed toIce King becoming the Winter King by forcing his madness onto Princess Bubblegum and turning her into the Candy Queen. Uncertain Doom: Downplayed as she's already long dead, but it's unclear if Betty died during the Mushroom War, for the vampires hunting humans, or if she was accidentally killed by Simon in a crazed state when he used the ice crown for the first time.

characters.name: The Candy Queen
characters.description: An alternate, insane, and monstrous version of Princess Bubblegum who terrorizes and kidnaps the Winter King on a regular basis. And I Must Scream:Bubblegum's conversation with Simon after turning back to normal implies that she was fully or at least partially conscious during her time as the Candy Queen, but unable to communicate with anyone about her situation. The Assimilator: She plans to throw herself, Simon, and the Winter King into a blender to forcibly fuse their bodies together. Ax-Crazy: She's a counterpart to the Ice King, after all, madness included. Her whole ploy is to blend herself with the Simons in a twisted declaration of love.Once the Winter King dies, she returns to normal. Evil Counterpart: Is introduced as a crazy evil version of Princess Bubblegum,except she's only like that because the Winter King transferred his madness to her.

characters.name: Finn
characters.description: An alternate version of Finn who is in a relationship with this universe's version of Slime Princess, and the champion of the Slime Kingdom. Adaptational Angst Downgrade: Unlike his main timeline and Farmworld counterparts, Winter World Finn seems much more well-adjusted and isn't tied down by tragedies. Adaptational Job Change:Impliedanddownplayed. Going by Winter World Princess Bubblegum calling himThe Championof Slime Kingdom and Finn declaring "Slime Time!" instead of "Adventure Time!", it's hinted that this version of Finn isn't a full-time adventurer like his main timeline self and instead serves the Slime Kingdom. Adaptational Upbringing Change:Implied. It is implied that this version of Finn was not adopted by Joshua and Margaret, or if Joshua and Margaret are slime people in this universe. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul:It is implied that this version of Finn never had a romantic interest in Candy Queen or Bonnie.This version of Finn appears to have married Slime Princess, while in the main timeline, they are friends.It is also implied that this version of Finn never had a romance with Huntress Wizard.

characters.name: Baby Finn
characters.description: An infantile version of Finn who ends up stowing away in Fionna's backpack and is accidentally brought with her, Cake, and Simon to the next world they visit. The Ageless: It’s confirmed he will never grow older, and possibly never die. Badass Adorable: In aBad FutureofFionna World, he's seen fighting against large butterflies, while still being a baby. This is after hundreds of years have passed. Improbable Infant Survival:He's left behind in the overturned Peppermint Tank halfway through "The Star" and is never seen or mentioned even after Fionna, Cake, and Simon jump to the next world, leaving his fate unknown. Fortunately, "Cheers" reveals him to still be alive, and he gets brought to Fionna World alongside Pep Tank.Exaggeratedin theBad Futurewhere Kaiju-sized "biterfiles" roam Fionna World. He's the only one seen alive...afterhundreds of years. He's left behind in the overturned Peppermint Tank halfway through "The Star" and is never seen or mentioned even after Fionna, Cake, and Simon jump to the next world, leaving his fate unknown. Fortunately, "Cheers" reveals him to still be alive, and he gets brought to Fionna World alongside Pep Tank.

characters.name: The Star
characters.description: A version of Marceline who is gleefully cruel and murderous to all but her "dad" the Vampire King, including the other vampires. Action Fashionista: A villainous example, as she fights while wearing ornate dresses. Adaptational Upbringing Change: In this timeline, Marceline never met Simon. Instead, she is raised by the Vampire King. Adaptational Wimp:Implied. This version of Marceline has only demonstrated the power of the Fool'sflightand the Hierophant'sshapeshifting. Also, in this universe, the Vampire King is still alive; therefore, this version of Marceline lacks hertelekinesis. It is unknown whether she also lacks theInvisibilityof the Empress or theHealing Factorof the Moon. Bad Boss: She joyfully poofs her own servants just for saying something that irks her, and scares another into poofing themselves.

characters.name: The Vampire King
characters.description: A version of the Vampire King who found the Ice Crown after Simon's death and used it to create clouds to blot out the sun, allowing his vampires to hunt 24/7. The Corrupter: He's why the Marceline of this universe is much more villainous than her main counterpart. Curb-Stomp Battle: He effortlessly defeats and kills Huntress without so much as a scratch. Didn't Think This Through: As Bonnie points out,he and his fellow vampires' overhunting of humansmeans they no longer have a sustainable food source, which does not bode well for his species' survival. It's implied, however, thathe isn't exactly in his right mind anymore to realize and/or care about this due to the crown's influence. Drunk with Power: Due to the power granted by the Ice Crown to completely control humidity on a planetary scale to create an artificial eternal night.

characters.name: Bonnie
characters.description: The leader of the only resistance to the rule of the Vampire King and the Star. Anti-Hero: Although her goal is the noble quest to liberate Ooo from the Vamps, she is even more ruthless and calculating than Prime Timeline Bubblegum. The only reason she even stops to help Fionna, Simon, and Cake is because of Cake's mutant stretchy powers. Boyish Short Hair: Bonnie wears her gum hair in a military flattop as part of her militaristic look. Eyepatch of Power: The Star took Bonnie's right eye, with the latter wearing an eyepatch to cover up the wound. Failure Hero: It is implied that her attempts to destroy the Vampire King and his followers were unsuccessful for centuries.

characters.name: Huntress
characters.description: A human version of Huntress Wizard. Alternate Species Counterpart: Huntress is a human version of Huntress Wizard, and as such possesses Hunter's skin and hair. Badass Normal: She doesn't have any of her Ooo counterpart's magic, but is still very skilled with a bow and arrow and a capableStealth Expert. Human Pincushion: She dies from being impaled by her own arrows off-screen in a worthless attempt to kill the Vampire King. Killed Offscreen: Her death wasn't shown, with the Vampire King carrying her deceased corpse after Bonnie's plan failed.

characters.name: Peppermint Tank
characters.description: An A.I.-controlled tank used by Bonnie's crew to traverse the wastelands of the Vampire World. Abnormal Ammo: Because Bonnie's crew is fighting a legion of vampires, the tank fires wooden stakes like missiles, and they use garlic for bombs and arrowheads. Alternate Species Counterpart: Prime Universe Pep was a sentient peppermint candy. The Peppermint Tank is justPeppermint Butler, but as a tank. Interspecies Adoption:Implied. The fact that he had to ask Fionna to babysit Baby Finn (so he could party) and that Fionna later asks Elias P. to take the baby back to him suggests Peppermint Tank has become Baby Finn's main caretaker ever since arriving in Fionna World. Sapient Tank: An A.I. in the form of a tank who is just as sentient as everyone else.

characters.name: The Ice King
characters.description: A version of the Ice King whose abandoned tapes leave a clue to what happened to this world. Apocalyptic Log: His tapes, albeit accidentally, with the Ice King (and Fionna and Cake for that matter) not knowing that he wouldbe instantly reduced to a skeleton as a result of the Lich's wish to end all life. As a result, they capture his and Gunter's last moments. Call-Back: In one of the tapes, the Ice King sings a bad parody of "Everything Stays" involving bagels and cream cheese. Dead Alternate Counterpart: This version of Ice King diedwhen the Lich turned all people of his universe into skeletons. Posthumous Character: He's long dead, with even the Ice Kingdom having melted away into a pile of his broken former belongings.The Lich even ends up mistaking Simon for him, thinking that he somehow managed to resurrect himself.

characters.name: Fionna Campbell
characters.description: An immature and somewhat self-centered 29-year-old woman living in a mundane world with her pet cat, Cake. Feeling stuck in an empty and monotonous life, she dreams of becoming a great adventurer. She eventually finds out from Prismo that she once lived in a magical world and that her entire world is in danger of being erased by the forces of the Multiverse, sending her on a quest to restore the magic and save her world before it's too late, with Cake becoming her sidekick in her adventures. Accidental Murder:During the events of "The Winter King" when Fionna kisses the titular character, she ends up somehow draining the magic crown he was using of its magic as he starts losing his magic and goes throughRapid Agingbefore turning to dust and dying. While it was unintentional, The Winter King was actually aBitch in Sheep's Clothingwho transferred his madness over to that universe's version of Princess Bubblegum for a century.Also due to the above, the minds of Gunther, Santa and Svein were erased from the crown when it lost its magical properties. Also due to the above, the minds of Gunther, Santa and Svein were erased from the crown when it lost its magical properties. Adaptational Angst Upgrade: Unlike Finn or even her previous magical self, Fionna in the Mundane World is basically a normal woman with problems like holding a job or earning money. In addition, Fionna's life in the Mundane World alsodoesn'tallow her to "put it in the vault" when it comes to encountering traumatic experiences, as seen in Season 2.

characters.name: Cake
characters.description: An ordinary cat living in a mundane world with her owner, Fionna. Adaptational Jerkass: She's noticeably more callous in this series. She neverquitereachesCats Are Meanlevel, but is often quiteInnocently Insensitiveand doesn't always have the best sense of what behavior is acceptable. Justified as shebecame a regular housecat after magic was drained from her universeand thus never had to learn manners. Later on, she has zero compunctions about handing the crown to Simon to allow magic back to her own universe, even if she knows it will turn him into the derangedCloud Cuckoolanderthat is the Ice King, as long as she gets to remain as she currently is, and even butts heads with Fionna about it. Adorable Fluffy Tail: Her tail is much fluffier than Jake’s. Animal Jingoism: Averted, as Cake doesn't seem to have any problems with dogs. She gets along famously with Farmworld Jake, even sneaking him food under the table, and enjoys hearing BMO's stories about her canine counterpart. She does somewhat dismissively refer to Prismo as a "dog person", though. Anthropomorphic Transformation: She goes from a realistically-proportioned cat to aFunny Animalwith a bipedal and egg-shaped body, courtesy of Prismo fixing her being "off-model".

characters.name: Gary Prince
characters.description: A barista and pastry chef working in Butterscotch Butler’s bakery. He plans to open his own pastry shop. Adaptational Angst Downgrade: Gary grew up in a normal family environment, while Bonnie had to fend for herself from childhood. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul:Gumball's relationship with Marshall Lee is antagonistic inAdventure Time, with Gumball vaguely listing Marshall Lee as one of his "regrets," implying that the two were once friends (or more) but had that friendship ended poorly. However, in this series, the two do not meet in the mundane universe until "The Winter King", where they almost immediately hit it off and begin to develop feelings for each other.Given that they're supposed to be the same characters as inAdventure Time, it's unclear if this is meant to mirror how their relationship began in the previous setting before things between them went sour.Gary's interactions with his parents are much more positive and loving than Princess Bubblegum's interactions with the Mother Gum. However, in this series, the two do not meet in the mundane universe until "The Winter King", where they almost immediately hit it off and begin to develop feelings for each other.Given that they're supposed to be the same characters as inAdventure Time, it's unclear if this is meant to mirror how their relationship began in the previous setting before things between them went sour. characters.name: Marshall Lee
characters.description: Spear Counterpartto Marceline, the Vampire Queen. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: Marceline and Finn are friends while their counterparts seem romantic. Either Marcy just wanted to tell a romance since the princesses would like it, she had some feelings for Finn, or Marshall has no romantic feelings and was just teasing as he is prone to joking more than his counterpart. Affably Evil: He plays the "Bad Boy" persona well, makes no secret of his heritage, andwillsummon the forces of the undead on you if he has to, but is overall aJerk with a Heart of Gold. All Girls Want Bad Boys: He believes that Fionna likes him because of this. Ambiguously Bi:Given that he's Marceline's counterpart. While he's never shown interest in boys in the show that's most likely since the story was made when Bubblegum and Marceline were rivals before they got back together. On the other hand, the comic series implies that there was something going on between him and Gumball in the past,but now they're trying to be friends.The show also vaguely hints at a past relationship between Marshall Lee and Gumball in "Five Tables Short" by having Gumball remember Marshall Lee as one of his "regrets".As of theAdventure Time: Fionna and Cakeseries he develops an immediate romantic attraction and relationship with Gary Gumball in the mundane version of their world after it loses their magic, causing them to in turn lose their memories of their former selves, implying that their romantichistory may be repeating itself all over again with a fresh start this time. Given that Marceline and PB are arguably theOne True Pairingin their universe, it's not hard to imagine Marshall and Gumball are each other's as well.

characters.name: DJ Flame
characters.description: The mundane universe equivalent of Flame Prince. He is also Fionna's ex-boyfriend. His real name is Phelix Principio. Adaptational Jerkass: Implied and later subverted. While he seemed like a decent guy in his original fanfic appearances, DJ Flame breaks up with Fionna via a two-word text message in the opening sequence. However, when we see him in Season 2, he’s a decent guy who appears to have genuinely liked Fionna while they were dating, and post-breakup, he treats her like a friend and is willing to help her save The Sweet Spot. Then double subverted when he kisses Fionna after Boys' Night...in front of Fennel and Hunter. Ambiguously Evil: While "evil" is a strong word to apply to Phelix, he's all over the place regarding his relationship with Fionna. Before the show, he had a steady relationship with Fionna for half a year, only to have herDumped via Text Messageout of the blue. Upon interacting with Fionna again in Season 2,Phelix still acts quite nicely to Fionna but doesn't acknowledge his insensitive break-up with her through a text message, and also acts rather suggestively intimate in his interactions with her despite dating Fennel at the moment, which causes Fionna to believe that he still has feelings for her.Not helping matters is Phelix returning Fionna's kiss in "The Insect That Sang", and when Fennel ends up witnessing this moment and runs off crying, Phelix chases after while attempting to say that what happened between him and Fionna "didn't mean anything". Tellingly, Phelix is implied to have only dated Fennel in the first place because of her being identical to Fionna. Ambiguous Situation: Why did he break up with Fionna in the first place, and why couldn’t he do it in person? Ascended Extra: In the first season, he only appears very briefly and has no lines. In the second season, he plays a major role. We see that Fionna still has feelings for him, how they met and fell in love, and how they get along post-breakup. Although he has moved on, he

characters.name: Beatrice Buttler
characters.description: The human counterpart of Butterscotch Butler. She is the crotchety owner of Butler’s Buttery Buns, the bakery where Gary Prince works. Adaptational Relationship Overhaul: She is subservient to Prince Gumball in the fanfic universe. However, in the mundane setting, she is his crotchety boss. Appeal to Tradition: She refuses to allow Gary to sell his own baked goods because she believes her traditional buttery buns are superior without even trying his work. She also allows mice to roam around her bakery because it is supposedly customary. Mean Boss: To prove that her traditional buttery buns are superior to Gary's pastries, rather than tasting it, she drops one on the floor and lets a mouse decide which one it prefers. She also repeatedly pokes Gary in the torso to emphasize her point about "traditional" being better. The Napoleon: She wears platform heels to make herself appear taller than she actually is and has quite the attitude, especially toward Gary Prince.

characters.name: Hunter
characters.description: A humanSpear Counterpartof Huntress Wizard. Above the Influence: Hunter is unwilling to take advantage of an emotionally vulnerable and drunk Fionna when she tries to kiss them. Adaptational Curves: Compared to Huntress Wizard, they have a much more muscular build. Adaptational Gender Identity: “The Wolves Who Wandered” confirms that Hunter is nonbinary and uses they/them pronouns, while Huntress is consistently female and uses she/her pronouns. Berserk Button: A small one. But upon meeting Huntress Wizard for the first time and hearing her call them "soft and weak", Hunter becomes very offended despite being calm. Given what Fennel implies about Hunter's past in the next episode, it's clear that Huntress' words hit a sore spot.

characters.name: Ellis P.
characters.description: The human counterpart of Lumpy Space Prince. A self-proclaimed animal miracle worker who is friends with Marshall. Animal Lover: He loves animals of all kinds. Berserk Button: Seeing animals abused or imprisoned really makes him angry. Gut Feeling: He's a big fan of relying on his "instincts" instead of actually thinking things through, even advising Fionna to go with her gut more... but the problem is that hisGut Feelingis neither as accurate nor as reliable as he himself thinks. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Like his counterpart, he's obnoxious and full of himself, but isn't abadguy. He's a genuineNature Loverand by all accounts a good friend to Marshall. He truly wants to help out, even if his help tends to either not be much use or even make things worse.

characters.name: Lemoncarb Twins
characters.description: The human counterparts of the Lady Lemongrabs. They are a pair of wealthy sisters known for running a food empire and making businesses flourish with their investments. Adaptation Species Change: Their equivalent to Lemon Camel is a yellow dog with a similarly droopy face. Canon Foreigner:Downplayed. The original Lady Lemongrabs never appeared in the original TV series and have only ever appeared in the comics. Their human forms marks the twins' first animated appearance. The Dividual: They're never seen apart and have the exact same erratic personality; they might as well be two halves of the same person. They're not even given individual names. Hiding Behind Your Bangs: The Lemoncarb in white wears her hair covering half of her face and one eye,the same side of the head that was bitten off of Lemongrab 2.

characters.name: Queenie
characters.description: Ascended Extra: From a minor character who fires Fionna from her latest job in the tour bus in Season One, she becomes aCorrupt Corporate Executivewho antagonizes Fionna's group in Season 2. Big Bad Ensemble: One of the three of Season 2 alongside Witch Wizard and Hana Abadeer, as Queenie's takeover of the Sweet Spot is what drives the conflict for Fionna and her friends to raise the money to buy the property back. Big Bad Slippage: She started as a minor character who was Fionna'sMean Bossin the latest of odd jobs she had taken and gotten fired from in Season 1, to becoming one of the main antagonists of the second season by dangling the fate of Fionna's friend's dream job and living space. Corrupt Corporate Executive: Queenie is only looking out for her own personal gain and doesn't mind crushing the efforts of Fionna's friends to get ahead. Even Evil Has Standards: Queenie may be aMean Bossto Fionna, and aCorrupt Corporate Executivein general, but she was justifiably disgusted by Fionna'sDefiant Stripin Season 1.

characters.name: M-Cron
characters.description: Adaptational Romance Downgrade: He has no romance with Cake in the first season ofFionna & Cake, as he's become human while Cake is (initially) an ordinary housecat. This gets subverted in the second season ofFionna and Cakewhere both Cake and M-Cron are shown to be mutually attracted to each other,before it's implied to be double subverted with M-Cron being implied to be aRomantic False Leadwhile the Karmic Worm is Cake's trueLove Interest. Ascended Extra: Appears in the opening for Season 2 and has a larger role as Cake's crush, compared to his smaller role as Gary's candy supplier in Season 1. Better as Friends:With Cake at the end of Season 2. Interspecies Romance: With Cake in Season 2. Cake is a magical cat who can shapeshift, while M-Cron is an ordinary human. Karmic Transformation: Implicit. Considering that in the main timeline the Raincorns eat humans, M-Cron becoming human is karmic.

characters.name: Fennel
characters.description: Adaptational Relationship Overhaul:Her Ooo counterpart, Fern, never had any relationship to Flame Princess. Fennel, however, is dating DJ Flame.On the other side, Fionna herself confirms she's never even seen Fennel before season 2, meaning they have no relationship whatsoever, in contrast to Fern, who was a copy of Finn.She and Hunter are friends who've apparently known each other for many years, whereas Huntress Wizard only really knew Fern in his villainous Green Knight persona serving under Gumbald. Her Ooo counterpart, Fern, never had any relationship to Flame Princess. Fennel, however, is dating DJ Flame. On the other side, Fionna herself confirms she's never even seen Fennel before season 2, meaning they have no relationship whatsoever, in contrast to Fern, who was a copy of Finn. She and Hunter are friends who've apparently known each other for many years, whereas Huntress Wizard only really knew Fern in his villainous Green Knight persona serving under Gumbald. Ambiguously Bi: While she's dating DJ Flame, the “The Wolves Who Wandered” shows Fennel admiring Fionna. Towards the end of the episode the two get touchy-feely, albeit while high on Huntress Wizard's Wizard Eyes magic. When she sees Fionna kissing Phelix, she later admits she's less upset about Phelix cheating on her, and more upset that she thought she had made a real friend in Fionna. Notably, she paused before saying the word "friend", and her POV during the kiss focuses on Fionna, not Phelix.

characters.name: Ice Cream Queen
characters.description: Ice Queen's mundane counterpart, she works as an ice cream vendor. Her real name is Simone. Adaptational Angst Downgrade: Zigzagged. Unlike Simon, Simone didn't have to deal with a magic artifact that slowly drives her insane, nor did she have to go through the end of a civilization. Simone is also implied to have also dealt with the loss of a loved one, but dealt with it healthily by being aFriend to All Children. However, Simone's bond with Marshall is cut short when she getsMistaken for Pedophileby Hana and forced to keep her distance from him for years. Adaptational Backstory Change: In the Fanfic World, she's (possibly) not a counterpart to Simon Petrikov, being awater nymph transformed into the Ice Queen according to the comics.The Mundane World has her mirror Simon more clearly, with a similar name, white eyes, similar skin color, and a familiarity with Marshall Lee, Marceline's counterpart. She's even juxtaposed as the Simon counterpart in the Season 2 opening, and the reason why Cake and Fionna ended up in Ooo was due to Simon's portal being created in Ice Cream Queen's cart.It's heavily implied that since Ice King has permanently reverted to Simon, when the Fanfic World transformed into the Mundane World, Simone ends up taking onSimon'straits. Adaptational Job Change: In the main timeline, Simon was an archaeology professor specializing in ancient artifacts while Simone is an ice cream vendor. Adaptational Nice Guy: The Ice Queen of the Fanfic World was a cruel mistress, even compared to the Ice King. In the Mundane World, since Simone is Simon's counterpart instead, she's much nicer in general.

characters.name: Damon
characters.description: Adaptational Job Change: In the main timeline, Damon was an jailer of demons while Fionna world is a Hana's spy. Mysterious Protector: An unwanted case, since he's on Hana's payroll. He acts as her eyes to ensure Marshall isn't in danger, and his surveilance of Simone ended with Hana filing a restraining order against her for Marshall. Marshall never finds out until adulthood. Nice Job Breaking It, Hero!: Damon misinterpreting the situationof the friendship of Marshall and Simone. He informs Hana of Marshall and Simone's interactions, which culminates in Hana filing a restraining order and them cutting off contact for years. Paper-Thin Disguise: Most of his disguises are not convincing, such as his pigeon costume, which is still the size of a human. Punny Name: His name is basically one letter away from "Demon", and his main Ooo counterpart is a demon while he serves as Hana's spy.

characters.name: The Cast Of Cheers
characters.description: Affectionate Parody: They're little guys that tease the sense of humor the originalCheersdid, having very brief snippets of snark, moping around, and unity. Ascended Extra: WhileCheerswas established in "Simon and Marcy", the cast itself were never seen or mentioned.Fionna and Cakewould not only present their own version of the show, but have Cake briefly interact with the cast in Season 2. Celebrity Impersonator: They are the spitting images ofnotein titles orderTed Danson,Rhea Perlman,John Ratzenberger,Kelsey Grammer(during theoriginal series' run, so he has hair),andGeorge Wendt(in the show's art style), suggesting that they were ported over from Simon's memories. Lilliputians: Every television actor in Fionna-world is 3 inches tall. Riddle for the Ages: Where did they come from and why are they so tiny? The show never answers this, but only because everyone in Fionna World (except Cake) treats it like this is perfectly normal. Although it is implied that they were exported directly from Simon's memories.

characters.name: Frank
characters.description: Hunter's implied manager in the city park. Ambiguous Situation: Why Frank is aJerkass to Onein regards to Hunter is currently unknown, whether it's because of a personal grudge, a rivalry,simply because he can, or if he'sbigotedtowards Hunter's non-binary status. The Ghost: So far, Frank has only been mentioned by Hunter in a flashback during Season 2. Jerkass Has a Point:Deconstructed. Granted, Frank does have a legitimate reason to give Hunter flak for Fionna's no-show at the park meeting despite them recommending her (not helping with the rumor that she ran around in a grocery store buck naked when it was actually Huntress Wizard), but since he's implied to be aMean Bossto Hunter in general, it only adds more stress to them. Jerkass to One: While it's unknown if Frank is a jerkass to other workers, he specifically singles out Hunter, as mentioned by the latter in a flashback.

characters.name: Queen of Venus
characters.description: The Queen of the Venusians. Barbie Doll Anatomy: She has no visible nipples due to her body being made of stone.

characters.name: Venus Cantrix
characters.description: A Venusian citizen who is first encountered by Fionna. Friend to All Living Things: Cantrix demonstrates her love by not stepping on an insect. Love at First Punch: She immediately proposes to Fionna after being accidentally slapped by her. Though she quickly calls off the engagement when Fionna invokes a duel with her leader to save DJ Flame. Pink Means Feminine: She wears a pink attire and is very feminine and love-obsessed. Vocal Dissonance:Downplayed. She's an adult like Fionna and Fennel, but Cantrix speaks in a rather husky voice despite her shorter appearance.

characters.name: Venus Cosmic
characters.description: The Love Champion of Venus. Robotic Reveal: Fionna and Fennel kick her head off, revealing her to be a robot.

characters.name: Fionna
characters.description: Finn'sGender Flipcounterpart who is considerably more level-headed than he is. She still manages to have a thirst for adventure, however. Action Dress Rip: When she has to fight Ice Queen while wearing a ball gown. Cakehilariously mistakes this for something else. Action Girl: She's shown to be a good fighter like her male counterpart, especially when battling Ice Queen. Ambiguously Bi: Fionna is for the most part shown to be completely straight, as everyone she shows open attraction to is male. That said the first time she met Princess Bubblegum she was blushing the whole time. Attractive Bent-Gender: She's Finn's female counterpart and is pretty and curvaceous, especially compared to Finn's more blocky figure.

characters.name: Prince Gumball
characters.description: Princess Bubblegum'sGender Flipcounterpart. Adaptational Name Change: In theAdventure Time: Fionna and Cakeseries, his nameafter magic was drained from his universeis "Gary Prince." Amazing Technicolor Population: In theAdventure Time: Fionna and Cakeseries,after magic was drained from his universehe notably still has pink skin despite everyone else being given more human skin tones. His pink hair is dyed, however. Amazon Chaser: Attracted to Fionna both for her strengthandbeauty.However this was actually Ice Queen in disguise and simply flattering Fionna into a trap, but the real deal also thinks she is 'incredible' when fighting. Ambiguously Bi:Given that he's PB's counterpart. While he has never shown interest in boys in the primary series, this is very likely due to his story being made when Bubblegum and Marceline were still rivals prior to them getting back together as a couple.As of theAdventure Time: Fionna and Cakeseries he develops an immediate romantic attraction and relationship with Marshall Lee in the mundane version of their world after it loses their magic, causing them to, in turn, lose their memories of their former selves, implying that their romantichistory may be repeating itself all over again with a fresh start this time. Given that Marceline and PB are arguably theOne True Pairingin their universe, it's not hard to imagine Marshall and Gumball are each other's as well.In "Five Tables Short", it's revealed that Marshall Lee is one of Gumball's "regrets", though the episode doesn't clarify what was meant by this.A bit more emphasis is put on their relationship in the graphic novel series, and it's similarly implied thatsomethingis going on between Marshall Lee and Gumball, as the two hang out with each other with little animosity shown between them.There's also the instance in the comic where Marshall Lee confronts Gumball about being invited to his party, and they have this questionable exchange.

characters.name: Lumpy Space Prince
characters.description: The handsome, charmingly suave, and generous prince of Lumpy Space. Depending on the Writer:In-universe. In Marceline's rendition of the Ice King's fanfic,LSPrinceis (invokedunsurprisingly) theexact same characterasLSPrincess, only with a peach-fuzz mustache. Odd thing is: this is only LSP's second appearance (he first appeared in "Adventure Time with Fionna and Cake" in a non-speaking role). It wouldn't be until his 3rd appearance that gave him character development and turned him into what is essentially the exact opposite of LSP's personality.The actual episode reveals that Ice King also views him as virtually identical to LSP and the suave, sophisticated portrayal he gets in the episode is only because LSPforcedhim to alter the character. In-universe. In Marceline's rendition of the Ice King's fanfic,LSPrinceis (invokedunsurprisingly) theexact same characterasLSPrincess, only with a peach-fuzz mustache. Odd thing is: this is only LSP's second appearance (he first appeared in "Adventure Time with Fionna and Cake" in a non-speaking role). It wouldn't be until his 3rd appearance that gave him character development and turned him into what is essentially the exact opposite of LSP's personality. The actual episode reveals that Ice King also views him as virtually identical to LSP and the suave, sophisticated portrayal he gets in the episode is only because LSPforcedhim to alter the character. Her Code Name Was "Mary Sue": When LSP dictates his story, he goes from the exact same person as her to a smooth-voiced, cool gentleman. This is less becauseshesees herself this way, and more because she was giving her counterpart all the traits of her dream guy in the case that Ice King could make him real.

characters.name: Lord Monochromicorn
characters.description: Lady Rainicorn'sGender Flipcounterpart and Prince Gumball's loyal companion. Speaks only in Morse Code. In a relationship with Cake. Affectionate Nickname: Prince Gumball sometimes calls him "Mo-Chro." Bilingual Bonus: Only talks in Morse Code. He does this by stomping and pawing at the ground. Cool Horse: Both him and his female and rainbow counterpart. Dark Is Not Evil: He looks like the mount of aBlack Knight, but he's a great guy.

characters.name: Ice Queen
characters.description: Ice King'sGender Flip, who also manages to look thirty years younger than him. Instead of the trademark crown, she wears a tiara instead. Abhorrent Admirer: Her obsession with Prince Gumball mirrors Ice King's habit of kidnapping Princess Bubblegum, with Gumball finding Ice Queen just as repellent. Adaptational Backstory Change: According to Gunter's version of events,she was a kindly person before she went mad, but she's not a variant of Simon, nor does she have a Betty equivalent; She was already magical, being a water nymph, but she went insane when a cat she befriended accidentally used a madness-inducing jewel to revive her instead of slowly being driven insane by a crown in the 20th century. Amulet of Concentrated Awesome: If she loses her tiara, she loses all her powers. Attractive Bent-Gender: Best example out of all the genderbent characters, as she appears taller and much younger than the actual Ice King and wears a beautiful blue gown. Justified, as not only does she exist in a fanfiction of his creation, butaccording to Gunter she didn't go through the same decades-long process of insanity Simon did.It's also because Natasha Allegri, who designed her, has said thatshe finds attractive villains far more unsettling than ugly ones.

characters.name: Ice King
characters.description: As Himself: In-universe example. Unlike the other storytellers who alter their counterparts when they tell their story, Ice King portrays himself with his normal mannerisms. Decomposite Character: Ice Queen was meant to be his counterpart in the genderbend universe, but Ice King is portrayed as separate from her.

characters.name: Lady Lemongrabs
characters.description: The genderbent counterparts to the Lemongrabs. They are quite similar to the originals, but are noticeably sexier... Well, slightly. The two debuted in the third issue of the Fionna and Cake comics, in the 2-page ministory "Sour Candy" by Kate Leth. Abusive Parents: While not outright abusive, Lady Lemongrab isn't the most... competent mother. She frequently yells harshly at her children when making simple requests or statements, and even ties up one of them in ribbon, even as the little thing wiggles in protest. Throughout their debut comic, the lemon children seem very unhappy, and their moms are oblivious to this. Alliterative Name: Rather than referring to themselves as countesses, they call themselves "Lady Lemongrabs." All Lesbians Want Kids: Beingpsycho lesbianscertainly didn't stop the Lady Lemongrabs from wanting to have children - or succeeding in their reproductive efforts! Attractive Bent-Gender: Kinda subtle. The Lady Lemongrabs don't look much different from the originals aside from the obligatory and silly tertiary sexual characteristics. But theydoappear to each have two butt cheeks (visible because they wear very tight pants,) unlike the original one-cheeked Lemongrabs.

characters.name: Dr. Prince
characters.description: Dr. Princess'Gender Flipcounterpart. A villain in one of Ice King's stories. Adaptational Villainy: Doctor Princess is a good-aligned character, but here he's apparently a villain for some reason.

characters.name: Flame Prince
characters.description: TheGender Flipof Flame Princess. Ambiguously Bi: Although some artwork depicts him as a potential new interest for Fionna,he also displays some heavily implied romantic feelings towards Turtle Prince in "Five Short Tables". Elemental Hair Colors: His hair is red and spiked-up to go with his nature as a fire elemental. Involuntary Shapeshifter: Turns into a little ball of flame when his temperature decreases too much. He can be touched in this form without injury. Mirror Self: Unlike Flame Princess, he's totally good and innocent from the start, thanks to being raised by animals instead of being kept as a prisoner in aDecadent Court.

characters.name: Tail Tufts
characters.description: TheGender Flipof Tree Trunks, as seen in the story "A Penny Burned" from the comic one-shotAdventure Time 2013 Summer Spectacular. Tertiary Sexual Characteristics: Resembles Tree Trunks, but has a mustache to indicate he is a guy.

characters.name: Butterscotch Butler
characters.description: A Scottish butterscotch butler. The gender-swapped version of Peppermint Butler. Brave Scot: She has a Scottish accent, and if she's anything like Pep-But is a force to be reckoned with. She's certainly a fierce and ruthless opponent when it comes to board games, according to "Five Short Tables". Department of Redundancy Department: When Gumball calls her, he calls her "Butterscotch Buttler, the butterscotch Scottish butler." Punny Name: Butterscotch Butler has a Scottish accent.

characters.name: Turtle Prince
characters.description: TheGender Flipof Turtle Princess. '80s Hair: His glam metal hairstyle sets him apart from his female counterpart. Ambiguously Gay:Unlike his female counterpart, he seems to be interested in Flame Prince rather than the opposite gender. Bookworm: Like Turtle Princess, he likes books. Ship Tease:"Five Short Tables" hints toward him and Flame Prince becoming a couple.

characters.name: Other fanfic characters
characters.description: Foil: He is this to Fionna. They are both heroic adventurers and fight off an evil wizard that has plans for their land. But while Fionna is an energetic Determinator who isn't afraid to speak her mind, Flynn is a stoic and extremely fancyFlat Characterwho has yet to get a speaking role or even aDay in the Limelight. Spear Counterpart: He serves as this to Fionna. Foil: He is this to Cake. They are both animal sidekicks to their human compatriots and help them with anything they come across. But while Cake is a sassy cat who isn't afraid to speak her mind as much as Fionna does if not more so, Jacques is a stoic and extremely fancyFlat Characterwho has yet to get a speaking role or evenA Day in the Limelightand doesn't even show off his shapeshifting powers. Spear Counterpart: He serves as this to Cake. Foil: He is this to the Ice Queen. They are both power-hungry villains who are even more cunning than the Ice King ever will be. But while the Ice Queen isThe Sociopath, the Ice President is more of anAnti-Villainand appears to be like a third to Flynn and Jacques' partnership.
